- Published
Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds has met the US-based owners of Poundland as the government hopes to save the retailer from collapse.
The discount chain is on the brink of insolvency and Gordon Brothers, which bought it for £1 last June, has rejected a takeover bid which could have saved the 12,000 jobs currently at risk.
A meeting was due to be held on Thursday but was brought forward as the scramble to secure a rescue deal for the firm intensifies.
Gordon Brothers said it is "pursuing all avenues through the sales process" but that Poundland has faced several years of instability and "remains challenged and vulnerable".
The firm said it is "engaging in active discussions on offers with interested parties".
It added: "When Gordon Brothers acquired the business, it was in distress and required a radical restructure, urgent operational change and significant funding, which we provided to support the company's ability to trade."
Both Reynolds and Prime Minister Andy Burnham have questioned why a deal for the future of the business has not been made.
On Wednesday, a source close to business secretary said Reynolds "has been firm that Gordon Brothers must do everything in their power to protect jobs and provide certainty for workers".
"He is pleased to have secured this commitment from Gordon Brothers in the meeting and will continue to hold the company to account and closely monitor developments," the source added.
It is understood that Gordon Brothers made a commitment in the meeting to prioritise bids that will protect workers and units.
However, it is still unclear whether the US investment firm will keep the business together or break it up.
Meanwhile, MPs say they have called in Poundland's owners for questioning on Wednesday 11 November to explain their role in the discount retailer's looming insolvency.
Liam Byrne, chair of Parliament's business committee, said: "Every report suggests Poundland is a viable, profitable business with a future ahead of it and without good reason to let it crash and burn - and then to break it up and sell it off piece by piece.
"We are asking Gordon Brothers to appear before Parliament to explain themselves and tell us just what it is that's preventing them from accepting the fully-funded deal on the table to save more than 12,000 jobs."
Business Minister Kate Dearden and union representatives met Poundland's managing director Barry Williams on Wednesday.
Mr Williams told the BBC that Poundland is profitable and sales were growing.
"We're back in profit and it has a bright future ahead of it if it's allowed to deliver that," he said.
Poundland has filed a notice of intention to appoint administrators, which protects it from its creditors until next Thursday.
Asked what his message for Poundland's owner was, Burnham said Gordon Brothers should "focus on the people in your employment" and "come up with a practical solution that saves jobs and saves those stores".
"There is a solution to be found here, sit down with us and let's find it," he added.
The meeting comes after a major Poundland supplier has said it will lose millions of pounds if the retailer goes bust.
Adam Turner, sales director at Bradford-based Highcrest Retail Brands, said Poundland was one of its biggest customers and its collapse would cost it "a few million" in lost sales.
The family owned business mainly sells confectionery to Poundland and turns over about £50m.
Turner said the firm becoming insolvent would leave a substantial gap in its balance sheet next year.
Highcrest was a "longstanding business that can stomach this", Turner said. But he warned other medium and small suppliers to the retailer have told him that "if Poundland goes under, so do they".
This echoes a warning from Poundland founder Steve Smith on Monday that two or three thousand suppliers to the firm, which only work for Poundland, would be directly affected by its collapse.
Not only would Poundland's 12,000 staff be affected in that case, but potentially up to 30,000 overall, he told the BBC on Wednesday.
He said he was "amazed" Poundland was being put into administration, pointing to the profitability of the company.
"Also, there's two offers on the table from some really good people," he added.
"All I'm asking is for Gordon Brothers to see if they can put a deal together."
Gordon Brothers said Walsall-based Poundland is "still not cash generative at a sustainable level" because of the economic issues it faces.
If Poundland's stores are sold to new buyers, some of the employees may get new jobs on the same premises.
However, it is understood that buyers are only interested in about half the stores at present – meaning roughly 6,000 employees would not be re-employed.
- Poundland's founder offers to invest in firm 
  - Published3 days ago
High stock levels
If Poundland goes under, suppliers will be getting "pennies in the pound" back from the administration, he said, which is "very upsetting" – although he still hopes a deal can be done so Poundland can remain solvent.
Poundland owners Gordon Brothers will be a secured creditor, which means they are first in line to get their money back, and suppliers "who have done nothing wrong" will take the financial hit.
"It's sad. It's a nightmare for us all to be honest with you. It's not just the suppliers, it's the staff at Poundland, some of these guys have been there for many years.
"It's from the warehouse staff all the way to the shop staff to everybody within head office. It's a massive ripple effect through the supply chain," he added.
Turner said he had no knowledge of whether Gordon Brothers had deliberately timed the process of Poundland going into administration so it could take advantage of having high stock levels, which it can then sell.
One of the ways Gordon Brothers makes money is through stock liquidations – selling off stock from collapsed businesses.
One insider familiar with the situation told the BBC that the timing of Poundland facing collapse was "odd" – most retailers don't fall over in the run-up to Christmas.
Ministers' questions
Dearden has said the government doesn't want to interfere with "current ongoing commercial negotiations", but that ministers want "clarity" on the plans for the retailer.
"It's absolutely legitimate for this government to ask the business if they're doing everything they can to protect employees and suppliers up and down the country," she added.
Dearden told MPs that the government would be ready to help the company's employees if Poundland collapses.
The head of Gordon Brothers' European operations reportedly told the government that the firm stood by its stewardship and had given Poundland £85m in additional financing since its purchase in 2025.

title: Liberal bus crashes into shop awning on its first outing of Victorian election campaign
content_c:
The Victorian Liberal party’s first offical day on the campaign trail has hit a snag, after its campaign bus reversed into the awning of a shopfront.
The “Jess Express”, a large blue bus emblazoned with an image of the opposition leader, Jess Wilson, was unveiled on Friday, 12 days after Labor launched its own red equivalent.
Featuring Wilson’s slogan, “A Fresh Start for Victoria”, the bus also carries a warning to motorists on its rear: “Dodging Labor’s potholes.”
But it wasn’t Labor’s potholes that brought the bus undone.
Arriving at Centre Road in Bentleigh for a street walk with Liberal candidate Tynan Putt, the bus was attempting to back into a parking spot when it struck the awning of a jewellery store, damaging the structure. The store was closed at the time.
Wilson grimaced as the incident unfolded, before quipping that the store’s owners wouldn’t have trouble finding the culprit, given her face was plastered across the side of the bus.
The Liberal campaign promptly contacted the store to provide its details, while the bus escaped with minor scratches. No one on board was injured.
The store’s owner, James Oppedisano, later told 3AW Radio that he had been out the back working on machine when the incident occurred.
“I … came back to my phone to find multiple missed calls from random numbers, including a text message from the Liberal party saying something about my awning. So that’s how I found out,” he said.
Oppedisano said he was yet to decide who to vote for but hoped fixing his awning would be an election promise that is actually delivered.
Just hours earlier, bus passengers – made up of Liberal party staff and reporters – read safety cards offering a “guide to surviving 12 years of Labor”.
Instructions included “please remain seated and brace for potholes”, “remain calm” in the event of a “financial emergency” and a warning that passengers may experience “motion sickness” due to “Labor’s constant spin”.
“Please look towards the fresh start on the horizon,” the cards read.
It’s not the first time a campaign bus has caused a political headache. During the final week of the 2025 federal election campaign, Peter Dutton’s bus became stuck after mounting a raised concrete divider and bike lane barrier on Pitt Street in the Sydney CBD.
The bus was stuck for about 40 minutes, causing traffic diversions and delaying the opposition leader’s schedule.
At the 2023 New South Wales state election, the then opposition leader Chris Minns opted for a zero-emissions bus that broke down after hitting a speed bump in western Sydney.
“I forgot to charge it last night and as a result it broke down,” Minns said at the time.
Journalists were promptly carted into a replacement, petrol-powered, bus.
In 2022, the Liberals in Victoria didn’t opt for a bus, instead debuting their “Ditch Danmobile” – a 1970s-style ambulance emblazoned with slogans.
Within an hour, the head of the Victorian Ambulance Union, questioned whether the stunt was legal, given state laws banning use of the word “ambulance” on any vehicle not owned or operated by an ambulance service without permission from the health department.
Current polling suggests the Coalition is well ahead of Labor, with the latest Newspoll putting it ahead 55-45 on a two-party-preferred basis.
The Liberals have Bentleigh firmly in its sights, despite Labor MP Nick Staikos holding the seat on an 8% margin. The electorate is considered a bellwether, having been won by the party forming government at 14 of the 16 elections since it was first contested in 1967.
Putt said the main issues in the electorate were cost of living and crime.
Victorians go to the polls on 28 November.

title: How irrational are Labour’s plans for migrant workers? To find out, read the small print | Frances Ryan
content_c:
If you want to see the senselessness of Britain’s immigration debate play out in real time, look no further than the crackdown on care workers’ visas that came to a head this week.
As part of its plans to force low-paid migrant workers to wait 15 years before settlement in the UK, the Home Office has been in a battle behind the scenes for the past six months to controversially include care workers in the policy. This is despite the social care system already facing critical staff shortages and the number of British citizens and immigrants taking the jobs dwindling.
After a fierce backlash from health unions and Labour cabinet members, this week the home secretary, Shabana Mahmood, announced a partial U-turn: an estimated 280,000 care workers and their dependents will be exempt and allowed to apply for indefinite leave to remain (ILR) after five years.
It’s a welcome reprieve from a policy that should never have been on the table. But check the fine print and this “watering down” will not protect every care worker. Only carers who earn £25,000 a year and entered or switched on to the care staff visa route before the white paper’s publication in 2025 will be eligible.
Those who don’t meet the strict requirements will have to get another five-year “health and social care” visa before applying for ILR – a move campaigners are warning will leave vulnerable workers open to exploitation from unscrupulous employers.
Ministers have not established what benefit any of this is meant to bestow on the British people, millions of whom rely on migrant carers to help them or their elderly parents wash and dress. Nor has anyone explained how Labour’s upcoming care reforms will work while alienating – rather than actively recruiting – more international staff, as recent tightened immigration rules already have.
Or, to put it another way: the government has simultaneously pledged to fix social care while creating a hostile environment for the migrant staff who keep the system afloat. It sums up not only the nastiness of it all, but the deep-seated irrationality that now plagues almost any mainstream conversation about immigration, with politicians across the spectrum seemingly contractually obliged to ignore basic common sense as well as decency.
Few things demonstrate this more than the obsession with the “contribution v cost” framing that dominates these debates, and which Labour has now threaded through its visa policy. On paper, it appears to many a fair and logical way to allocate visa rights. In practice, it rewards the wealthy and dismisses the value of working-class and predominantly female labour: while care workers will have to wait five or 15 years for ILR, a solicitor on £125,000 can get fast-tracked in only three. It is blatant classism, sure, but also fundamentally misses the very obvious tenet of capitalism that a worker’s “contribution” to a society and economy is not necessarily reflected in their wage packet.
That Mahmood has been doing the rounds in recent months using disputed figures to claim that granting ILR to care staff and their families for the next few years would cost the public purse £10bn over a lifetime suggests how unreliable – and outright ludicrous – the cost v contribution binary is. These are the people keeping our loved ones alive for the minimum wage and we’re still debating whether they’re a burden on the taxpayer.
Of course, evidence shows care workers are, to use that favoured phrase, “net contributors”. The Institute for Public Policy Research (IPPR) found this week that skilled migrants – including care workers – and their families due to settle in the UK under current rules are expected to boost the public purse by a staggering £115bn through taxes.
Such a figure doesn’t even include the many other ways care workers save the country money: by enabling family members to keep paying income tax rather than quitting their jobs to be an unpaid carer; supporting younger disabled people to get to the office and stay in work; or keeping older people out of expensive hospital beds by reducing their risk of falls.
And yet we are losing something if we accept the idea that a migrant’s “contribution” is only in economic terms, as if the Home Office can scan a human being at the border and put a price tag round their neck. Anyone who has ever relied on a good carer knows there is value that can’t be measured on a spreadsheet: the security of knowing there is someone to help you get out of bed in the morning; the dignity of having a regular shower; the laughter that comes with a shared joke as you write the shopping list together.
You won’t see many of these people on front pages or hear their voices on radio call-ins. But the people providing care and those who rely on it will “contribute” considerably more to the debate than the non-disabled white contrarians who so persistently dominate it.
If it is a “legitimate concern” for the public to worry about immigration, it is legitimate for a disabled person to be afraid there will be no one to help them cook dinner, or for a migrant to worry about where they’ll live next year.
Because here’s the thing about fears: some are irrational, and others are not. Labour would do well to remember which ones it should listen to and which it should challenge.
- 
  Frances Ryan is a Guardian columnist

title: Germany’s Gen Z protests spark debate on integration, bias
content_c:
Germany’s Gen Z protests spark debate on integration, bias
November 5, 2026
Responses to the violent scenes that followed recent Gen Z demonstrations in Germany have revealed differences in opinion within the federal government over who is responsible.
Though there is general agreement that people who committed acts of violence must be held accountable, some conservative lawmakers have largely blamed migrant groups — raising questions about whether they are reinforcing prejudice.
Leading Social Democrats have warned against generalizations, and at least one Cabinet minister from the Christian Democrats (CDU) would prefer to examine the causes of the violence. Gen Z's fears for the future are at threat of being overshadowed by the discussions in the government and the press's focus on scattered rioting.
In Frankfurt, more than 100 police officers were injured, one severely, in the street battles that erupted after the protest on October 31. Shops were damaged and looted, too. The situation in Cologne, Hamburg and Berlin also escalated.
That Saturday, tens of thousands of young people had taken to the streets across Germany for predominantly peaceful rallies. The initiative Gen Z regelt — which roughly means Gen Z takes charge — had urged young people to highlight their fears for the future and to call for better educational opportunities, affordable housing and more climate action.
CDU initially set tone of debate
German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt and Roman Poseck, the interior minister of Hesse, the state in which Frankfurt is located, quickly set the tone of the response. Most of those arrested were German citizens, said Poseck (CDU), but added: "This group of offenders was predominantly from a migrant background."
Dobrindt, who is from Bavaria's Christian Social Union, a party closely allied with Chancellor Friedrich Merz's CDU, said: "There were peaceful demonstrations, which into the evening were hijacked by violent left-wing groups and migrant hooligans."
Merz backed the statements made by Dobrindt. His assessment of the background of the offenders was based on "the observations of the investigating authorities and the emergency personnel on the ground," his spokesperson Stefan Kornelius said. It also matched "the images that many have seen."
Merz announced a tough approach toward the rioters. "Violence does not belong on our streets, and my government will show no tolerance here," Merz said, according to the script for a speech he was due to give at a closed-door CDU party event in Berlin on Monday (November 2). "Whoever attacks police and emergency services officers and loots shops attacks our freedom, ridicules society and the legitimate interests of young people."
Warnings against generalizations, focus on causes
The center-left Social Democrats (SPD), who are in a coalition government with the conservative CDU and CSU bloc, are in agreement on the point that criminals were involved. "It is criminals who attack and injure police officers and commit serious property damage," Defense Minister Boris Pistorius (SPD) told German public broadcaster ZDF on Sunday (November 1).
This is, however, where the similarities end. "What then are ‘migrant groups'?" said Pistorius, challenging the Interior Minister's choice of words. "Does that include people in the third generation living in Germany and who are German citizens? When do we stop drawing this distinction?" he countered. "I think that leads in the wrong direction."
The German federal government's integration commissioner, SPD politician Natalie Pawlik, followed up on Monday (November 2). "Always attributing such violent riots to migrant milieus is too simplistic," Pawlik told the German newspaper, the Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung. "Because blanket generalizations about groups also affect those with migrant backgrounds who demonstrated peacefully or who were themselves on duty with the police or emergency services."
She said nothing justified the outbreak of violence and that such crimes had to be punished. However, Pawlik added that if investigations showed that certain groups, in particular, were involved, then the root causes also had to be named. "We cannot ignore difficult questions about the lack of prospects, experiences of marginalization or possible integration problems," the integration commissioner said.
German Family and Education Minister Karin Prien (CDU) also wants to examine the causes of the violent behavior. She told German public radio broadcaster Deutschlandfunk that stirring resentment "would also be politically wrong." It is much more about reflecting upon reality. "If the (perpetrators) come from migrant backgrounds then that should cause us concern," Prien said.
According to Germany's Federal Statistical Office (Destatis), some 31% of the German population have a migration background. The proportion is higher in many big cities. The figure is over 50% in Frankfurt. Prien says it is necessary to examine why integration has been less successful in some groups of immigrants than others. The real challenge lies in facilitating societal participation and preventing parallel societies.
Risk of ban on Gen Z protests?
The political discussion was intensified by the Hesse interior minister suggesting a ban on further Gen Z protests. In respect of demonstrations planned for November 20, Poseck said that the right of assembly was very valuable, but social peace just as crucial. He said there had also been "massive attacks" against the police even during the demonstrations. "The organizers do not have these gatherings under control," he added.
The organizers of the demonstrations reject those accusations. They immediately distanced themselves from the violence. Germany's Family Affairs Ministry has announced that Karin Prien is due to meet with representatives from the Federal School Students Council (BSK) as well as the German Education Union (GEW) this week.
Prien herself called for younger people's interests to be taken into account more. "These are exactly the debates we need to be having, which young people are also very rightfully demanding," she told German public regional broadcaster RBB.
This article was originally written in German

"We cannot ignore difficult questions about the lack of prospects, experiences of marginalization or possible integration problems," the integration commissioner said.
German Family and Education Minister Karin Prien (CDU) also wants to examine the causes of the violent behavior. She told German public radio broadcaster Deutschlandfunk that stirring resentment "would also be politically wrong." It is much more about reflecting upon reality. "If the (perpetrators) come from migrant backgrounds then that should cause us concern," Prien said.
According to Germany's Federal Statistical Office (Destatis), some 31% of the German population have a migration background. The proportion is higher in many big cities. The figure is over 50% in Frankfurt. Prien says it is necessary to examine why integration has been less successful in some groups of immigrants than others. The real challenge lies in facilitating societal participation and preventing parallel societies.
Risk of ban on Gen Z protests?
The political discussion was intensified by the Hesse interior minister suggesting a ban on further Gen Z protests. In respect of demonstrations planned for November 20, Poseck said that the right of assembly was very valuable, but social peace just as crucial. He said there had also been "massive attacks" against the police even during the demonstrations. "The organizers do not have these gatherings under control," he added.
The organizers of the demonstrations reject those accusations. They immediately distanced themselves from the violence. Germany's Family Affairs Ministry has announced that Karin Prien is due to meet with representatives from the Federal School Students Council (BSK) as well as the German Education Union (GEW) this week.
Prien herself called for younger people's interests to be taken into account more. "These are exactly the debates we need to be having, which young people are also very rightfully demanding," she told German public regional broadcaster RBB.
This article was originally written in German

title: Pete Hegseth: Verteidigungsminister verteidigt Irankrieg und klammert sich an Amt
content_c:
US-Verteidigungsminister Hegseth verteidigt den Irankrieg – und klammert sich an sein Amt
Donald Trump hat es bereits sehr klar gemacht: Er sieht sich selbst – wenig überraschend – nicht in der Verantwortung für die Schlappe seiner Partei bei den Midterm-Wahlen in dieser Woche (mehr hier ). Doch wo lässt sich die Schuld dann abladen?
Nicht wenige in der konservativen Partei haben sich auf Verteidigungsminister Pete Hegseth eingeschossen. Dieser hat den Krieg gegen Iran nun vehement verteidigt und sich kämpferisch gegen eine drohende Amtsenthebung gezeigt.
In einer am Donnerstag (Ortszeit) veröffentlichten Videobotschaft bezeichnete er den Militäreinsatz als »mutig und historisch«. In dem vierminütigen Clip sagte Hegseth: »Die greifen mich und uns an, weil wir so effektiv sind. Das wird nicht funktionieren. Wir werden nicht nachgeben.« Spekulationen über eine Amtsenthebung zielten nur auf »persönliche Zerstörung« ab, so Hegseth: »Das hat gegen Präsident Trump nicht funktioniert. Und es wird gegen mich nicht klappen.«
US-Präsident Trump stellte sich bisher hinter seinen Minister und erklärte zuletzt, dieser habe fantastische Arbeit geleistet. Auf die Frage, ob er einen Abwechslung Hegseths erwäge, sagte Trump am Mittwoch vor Journalisten: »Nein, ich denke, er macht einen sehr guten Job.«
Insider sagten jedoch, Trump könne Hegseth ersetzen. »Hegseth könnte auf der Abschussliste stehen«, sagte ein Berater Trumps. »Jemand wird für die Wahlniederlage verantwortlich gemacht werden, und Sie wissen, dass das nicht Trump sein wird.« Hegseth gilt als maßgeblicher Befürwortes des Kriegs gegen Iran.
Der Vizepräsident hat sich schon einmal klar positioniert
Hegseth steht massiv unter Druck, nachdem Vizepräsident JD Vance den Irankrieg für die Wahlniederlage der Republikaner verantwortlich gemacht hatte (mehr hier). Auch Trump räumte ein, dass der Krieg und damit verbunden die rapide gestiegenen Spritkosten eine entscheidende Rolle bei der krachenden Niederlage gespielt habe. Der republikanische Abgeordnete Thomas Massie kündigte bereits ein Amtsenthebungsverfahren gegen Hegseth an.
Kritiker werfen dem Minister neben der Kriegsführung auch die Entlassung hochrangiger Militärs vor. Die Demokraten, die bei den Wahlen am Dienstag die Kontrolle über den Kongress gewonnen haben, planen ab dem kommenden Jahr weitreichende parlamentarische Untersuchungen gegen den Minister.
Die Frage ist zudem, wie es in dem festgefahrenen Irankonflikt nun weitergeht. Trump will über eine möglichen Wiederaufnahme des Krieges bald entscheiden. Erklärtes Ziel seines im Februar gemeinsam mit Israel begonnenen Krieges ist es, Iran am Bau einer Atombombe zu hindern. »Wollen wir noch weiter gehen« mit den Angriffen, damit »so etwas nie wieder passieren wird?«, sagte Trump Reportern im Weißen Haus.
»Ich würde den Rest des Landes lieber nicht zerstören, wenn möglich, aber vielleicht muss ich es tun«, sagte der Präsident und fügte hinzu, das würden »bald genug« klar werden.
Die Amerikaner haben ihren Präsidenten abgestraft, der Kampf um seine Nachfolge beginnt: Bei den Demokraten drängen junge Stars nach vorn, bei den Republikanern geht Vize Vance auf Abstand. Wie gefährlich werden Trumps letzte Amtsjahre? Die SPIEGEL-Titelstory.
description: Die Suche nach dem Sündenbock für die Wahlblamage der Republikaner läuft. Ein Kandidat: Pete Hegseth, als Verteidigungsminister eine treibende Kraft im Irankrieg. Und der gibt sich trotzig.

title: Marktbericht: DAX springt auf Rekordhoch
content_c:
Ölpreise beflügeln die Börse DAX auf Rekordkurs
Die Märkte bleiben im Aufwind: Nach den US-Zwischenwahlen erreicht der DAX im frühen Handel einen neuen Höchststand. Rückenwind erhält er von günstigeren Ölpreisen und positiven Signalen aus der Industrie.
Der DAX hat heute ein neues Rekordhoch erreicht, zeitweise stieg er auf einen Stand von rund 26.692 Punkten. Damit setzte der Leitindex seinen bereits am Mittwoch gestarteten Aufwärtstrend zunächst fort.
Am Nachmittag allerdings kamen negative Impulse von den US-Börsen. Während sich die Verluste bei Dow Jones Industrial und dem breiter gefassten S&P 500 einigermaßen im Rahmen hielten, kam es zu einem Ausverkauf bei Technologiewerten.
Die Sorgen über die Zukunft des KI-Sektors nach dem Wahlsieg der Demokraten in beiden Kammern des Parlaments belasteten den Nasdaq 100, der seine Verluste zeitweise auf sechs Prozent ausweitete. Das hinterließ auch beim DAX Spuren. Aus diesem Handelstag verabschiedete sich der Leitindex schließlich 0,4 Prozent tiefer bei rund 26.325 Punkten.
Wie lange diese grundsätzlich positive Börsenstimmung nach den Midterms aber anhalten wird, ist fraglich. Ökonomen mahnen, dass die erste Börsenreaktion nicht überinterpretiert werden dürfe.
In den vergangenen Jahrzehnten habe es in den Wochen nach den Midterms immer ein kräftiges Plus gegeben. "Die geopolitischen Unsicherheiten und das Risiko kräftiger Rückschläge bleiben bestehen", sagt Salah-Eddine Bouhmidi vom Broker IG.
Auch mit Blick auf die Ölpreise dürfte die Lage weiterhin unberechenbar bleiben. Diese sind in jüngster Zeit gesunken. Rohöl der Sorte Brent aus der Nordsee verbilligte sich innerhalb einer Woche um rund zwölf Prozent. Ein Barrel kostet inzwischen etwa 97 Dollar. Auch US-Öl der Sorte WTI ist aktuell mit rund 89 Dollar pro Fass günstiger und damit laut Datenanbieter Infront innerhalb einer Woche um etwas mehr als 13 Prozent gesunken.
Viele Investoren rechnen offenbar damit, dass eine friedliche Lösung für den Nahen Osten nun wahrscheinlicher geworden ist. Aber bisher gehen die gegenseitigen Angriffe weiter und eine diplomatische Lösung ist nicht in Sicht. Im Tagesverlauf zogen die Ölpreise dann wieder leicht an. Ökonomen gehen davon aus, dass Schwankungen beim Ölpreis weiter bestehen bleiben.
Marktanalyst Kyle Rodda bei Capital.com gibt zu bedenken: "Es gibt die Sorge, dass ein zunehmend geschwächter Präsident Trump außenpolitisch aktiver und möglicherweise riskanter agieren könnte, wenn er noch Einfluss nehmen will und weniger Gründe zur Zurückhaltung hat."
Sinken die Ölpreise dauerhaft, würde das den Inflationsdruck senken. Das würde auch die Gewinnaussichten für viele Unternehmen verbessern, weil die Produktionskosten günstiger werden.
Heute haben auch aktuelle Konjunkturdaten für Rückenwind an der Börse gesorgt. Die deutsche Industrie hat im September mehr Bestellungen erhalten und sich damit etwas vom Auftragseinbruch im Vormonat erholt. Das Neugeschäft legte um 4,4 Prozent zu, wie das Statistische Bundesamt (Destatis) mitteilte.
Commerzbank-Chefökonom Jörg Krämer spricht mit Blick auf die aktuellen Zahlen von einer positiven Überraschung: "Auch ohne die stark schwankenden Großaufträge zogen die Orders im September kräftig an. Damit steigt die Wahrscheinlichkeit, dass die Aufträge den Seitwärtstrend der zurückliegenden anderthalb Jahre verlassen und wieder steigen."
Zudem präsentierten wieder viele Unternehmen ihre Bilanzen. Darunter auch der DAX-Konzern Hochtief, der dank des KI-Booms kräftig verdient. Die Bücher des weltweit tätigen Baukonzerns sind nach zahlreichen neuen Aufträgen etwa für Rechenzentren so voll wie noch nie.
Die Deutsche Telekom ist im abgelaufenen Quartal vor allem dank ihrer US-Tochter T-Mobile US stark gewachsen. Umsatz und Gewinn legten stärker zu als von Experten erwartet. Das Unternehmen hob seine Prognose ein weiteres Mal leicht an.
Die vor der Übernahme durch die italienische Großbank UniCredit stehende Commerzbank hat im dritten Quartal deutlich mehr verdient und ihre Jahresziele bestätigt.
Das operative Ergebnis stieg im Vergleich zum Vorjahreszeitraum um 25 Prozent auf 1,31 Milliarden Euro, das Nettoergebnis kletterte um rund 45 Prozent auf 859 Millionen Euro. Beide Werte verfehlten jedoch knapp die durchschnittlichen Erwartungen der Analysten.
In den ersten neun Monaten kletterte der Überschuss ebenfalls um mehr als 40 Prozent auf rund 2,7 Milliarden Euro. Das ist das beste Ergebnis für diesen Zeitraum in der Konzerngeschichte. Für das Gesamtjahr peilt der Vorstand weiter einen Rekordgewinn von mindestens 3,4 Milliarden Euro an.
Verzögerungen bei Großaufträgen belasten derweil das erfolgsverwöhnte Rüstungsunternehmen Rheinmetall. Die Düsseldorfer mussten deshalb ihre Gewinnprognose senken und ihr Umsatzziel für 2026 erneut zusammenstreichen. Rheinmetall hatte bereits im August seine Umsatzprognose gesenkt, damals wegen des gestoppten F126-Fregattenprogramms.
Im dritten Quartal konnte Rheinmetall zwar erneut Wachstum ausweisen, dieses blieb beim Umsatz aber unter den Erwartungen des Marktes. Rheinmetall-Aktien erlebten heute ein Debakel: Die Papiere brachen zeitweise um mehr als 17 Prozent ein und waren mit Abstand größter Verlierer im DAX.
Und noch eine Nachricht aus dem Rüstungssektor stand heute im Fokus. Die Bundesregierung hat sich grundsätzlich mit den Eigentümerfamilien des Panzerbauers KNDS auf den Erwerb ihrer 50-prozentigen Beteiligung geeinigt. Das hat das ARD-Hauptstadtstudio aus Regierungskreisen erfahren. Damit will sich der Bund gemeinsam mit Frankreich, das die übrigen Anteile hält, Einfluss auf wichtige Schlüsseltechnologien sichern.

title: Bis zuletzt hat er dirigiert: Herbert Blomstedt ist im Alter von 99 Jahren gestorben
content_c:
Kleine Gesten mit großer Wirkung: Dirigent Herbert Blomstedt ist tot
5. November 2026
Er war ein Weltbürger, ein Dirigent mit Charisma, ein Meister der kleinen Gesten mit großer Wirkung. Wenn Herbert Blomstedt auf dem Podium stand, zog er das Publikum in seinen Bann, kein Konzert endete ohne Standing Ovations. Seine Orchestermusiker schätzten ihn als bescheidenen, charmanten und respektvollen Maestro fern jeglicher Starallüren.
Mit 99 Jahren war Blomstedt der dienstälteste international auftretende Spitzendirigent. Noch im hohen Alter gab er Konzerte in Europa, Japan und den USA. Nach einem Sturz im Juni 2022 dirigierte Blomstedt seine Konzerte nur noch im Sitzen. Beim Abschlusskonzert des Rheingau Musik Festivals im August 2023 ging er bereits sichtlich gebeugt und von einem seiner Musiker am Arm gestützt auf die Bühne, um Bruckners siebte Sinfonie zu dirigieren, eines seiner Lieblingsstücke. Danach wie immer: Standing Ovations im Publikum.
Ehrendirigent vieler Orchester
Seit mehr als 70 Jahren stand Herbert Blomstedt auf der Bühne. Viele Ensembles haben den schwedischen Dirigenten im Laufe der Jahre zum Ehrendirigenten ernannt. Darunter das San Francisco Symphony Orchestra, die Bamberger Symphoniker, die Wiener Philharmoniker sowie das NHK Symphony Orchestra in Tokio.
Blomstedt wurde am 11. Juli 1927 als Sohn schwedischer Eltern in den USA geboren. Der Vater war ein adventistischer Pastor, seine Mutter Pianistin. In Stockholm studierte Blomstedt Geige, in New York Dirigieren, in Tanglewood arbeitete er mit Leonard Bernstein zusammen. Blomstedt war vielseitig interessiert. Mit Renaissance- und Barockmusik beschäftigte er sich in Basel, mit der Neuen Musik des 20. Jahrhunderts in Darmstadt. In seiner Anfangszeit arbeitete er als Chefdirigent bedeutender skandinavischer Orchester.
Blomstedts Beziehung zu Deutschland
Von 1975 bis 1985, noch vor dem Fall der Mauer, die bis 1989 Ost- und Westberlin teilte und die damalige DDR von der Bundesrepublik Deutschland trennte, wurde er Chefdirigent und später Generalmusikdirektor bei der Staatskapelle Dresden. Anschließend übernahm er für zehn Jahre die musikalische Leitung des San Francisco Symphony Orchestra.
Dass ein Westeuropäer noch zu DDR-Zeiten die Stelle als Generalmusikdirektor bei einem ostdeutschen Orchester annahm, erregte damals Aufsehen. "Ich habe lange gezögert in einer kommunistischen Diktatur Chefdirigent zu werden", sagte Herbert Blomstedt in einer Ansprache, die er im November 2018 in der Dresdener Semperoper hielt. Das Orchester aber habe ihn fasziniert. Anlass der Rede war ein Solidaritätskonzert gegen rechte Gewalt mit der Staatskapelle Dresden und dem Gewandhausorchester Leipzig. Rechtsradikale hatten in Chemnitz randaliert und regelrecht Jagd auf Migranten gemacht.
Der "Leipziger Volkszeitung" sagte Blomstedt in diesem Zusammenhang: "Wir als Musiker erreichen nur eine begrenzte Anzahl an Menschen. Das bedeutet aber nicht, dass wir schweigen dürfen und damit den Schreihälsen das Feld überlassen. Im Gegenteil, es ist wichtig, dass wir Farbe bekennen. Ich glaube schon, dass dieses Zeichen wahrgenommen wird. Musik hat eine verbindende Kraft."
Brückenbauer Herbert Blomstedt
Der sächsischen Region war der Dirigent sein Leben lang verbunden. In der Nachfolge von Kurt Masur leitete er von 1998 bis 2005 das Gewandhausorchester in Leipzig. Sowohl die Staatskapelle Dresden als auch das Gewandhausorchester haben Herbert Blomstedt zu ihrem Ehrendirigenten ernannt.
Für sein Lebenswerk und für das herausragende Engagement um die „Pflege internationaler kultureller Beziehungen" erhielt Blomstedt 2022 die höchste Auszeichnung der Bundesrepublik Deutschland, das "Große Verdienstkreuz mit Stern". Sachsens Ministerpräsident Michael Kretschmer würdigte Blomstedt bei der Verleihung als einzigartige künstlerische Persönlichkeit. "Er ist ein Brückenbauer im besten Wortsinn und unterstreicht damit auch die verbindende Brückenfunktion der Kultur in Europa und der ganzen Welt."
Musik als Lebenselixier
Wenn man Herbert Blomstedt nach seinem Rezept für sein hohes Alter fragte, antwortete er, dass er die Kraft aus dem Glauben an Gott, seiner gesunden Lebensweise und der klassischen Musik schöpfe. "Die Musik - und damit meine ich die große klassische Tradition - gibt sehr viel Kraft, weil sie den Intellekt und die Emotionen gleichfalls stimuliert", sagte der Dirigent 2021 im DW-Interview.
Johann Sebastian Bach war Blomstedts Idol. Bruckners vierte Sinfonie hatte ihn schon als Schüler begeistert. Auch um die Komponisten seiner Heimat Schweden und der nordischen Länder hat er sich verdient gemacht. Die Sinfonien von Jean Sibelius und Carl Nielsen hat er ebenso eingespielt wie die Sinfonien von Beethoven, Bruckner und Schubert.
Der bescheidene Maestro Blomstedt
Dass er ein gefeierter Dirigent war, schien Herbert Blomstedt nicht sonderlich zu interessieren. Seine Bescheidenheit ehrte ihn, einen autoritären Führungsstil hatte er nicht nötig. So reiste er bei den Tourneen oft mit dem Orchester im Bus und verlangte in Hotels keine Sonderbehandlung.
"Die Energie, die von dem Dirigenten kommt, ist eine geistige Energie. Das soll nicht eine physische Energie sein - die bringt das Orchester selbst. Aber die geistige Energie! Die braucht einen einigenden Willen. Wenn der nicht da ist, verliert die Musik an Seele", sagte Herbert Blomstedt anlässlich seines 95. Geburtstags dem Norddeutschen Rundfunk (NDR). Beim NDR-Sinfonieorchester war er lange Gastdirigent und Ende der 1990er Jahre kurze Zeit auch Chefdirigent.
Seine fachliche Kompetenz und seine Genauigkeit, mit der er immer wieder die Partituren studierte, brachten ihm große Anerkennung in Fachkreisen. Bruckners Siebte hatte er schon oft dirigiert und kannte sie auswendig, dennoch beschäftigte er sich immer wieder aufs Neue mit der Partitur. "Ich mache viele Notizen, denn ich studiere die Partituren sehr genau, damit jede Note ihren besonderen Sinn bekommt", sagte er dem NDR.
Das Geheimnis eines langen Lebens
Herbert Blomstedt war zwar in den letzten Jahren körperlich gebrechlich, aber geistig fit. Zeit seines Lebens war der Maestro Vegetarier, Nichtraucher, trank keinen Alkohol und praktizierte Yoga. Blomstedt war bekennender Siebenten-Tags-Adventist. Sein Glaube an Gott spielte eine wichtige Rolle in seinem Leben. "Ich habe das Glück gehabt, in einer sehr gläubigen Familie aufzuwachsen. Jeden Tag wurde aus der Bibel vorgelesen und gebetet. Ich bin in dieser Atmosphäre aufgewachsen und das begleitet mich bis heute", sagte er der DW im Jahr 2021.
Immer wieder erzählte Blomstedt von seinen wunderbaren Eltern, seinem Bruder, von dem er viel gelernt habe, und von seiner Frau Waltraud, die ihm eine große Stütze gewesen war und ihn bei jedem seiner Konzerte begleitet hatte. Waltraud Blomstedt, mit der Herbert Blomstedt vier Töchter hat, starb bereits 2003.
Dirigieren, so sagte Blomstedt, wollte er solange er körperlich und geistig noch dazu in der Lage sei; und solange seine Orchester Freude daran hätten. "Ich möchte nicht irgendwann das Gefühl haben, dass die Freude nur auf meiner Seite ist." Laut Berichten seiner Agentur starb Herbert Blomstedt zu Hause in Göteborg im Kreis seiner Familie.

Wenn Herbert Blomstedt auf dem Podium stand, zog er das Publikum in seinen Bann, kein Konzert endete ohne Standing Ovations. Seine Orchestermusiker schätzten ihn als bescheidenen, charmanten und respektvollen Maestro fern jeglicher Starallüren.
Mit 99 Jahren war Blomstedt der dienstälteste international auftretende Spitzendirigent. Noch im hohen Alter gab er Konzerte in Europa, Japan und den USA. Nach einem Sturz im Juni 2022 dirigierte Blomstedt seine Konzerte nur noch im Sitzen. Beim Abschlusskonzert des Rheingau Musik Festivals im August 2023 ging er bereits sichtlich gebeugt und von einem seiner Musiker am Arm gestützt auf die Bühne, um Bruckners siebte Sinfonie zu dirigieren, eines seiner Lieblingsstücke. Danach wie immer: Standing Ovations im Publikum.
Ehrendirigent vieler Orchester
Seit mehr als 70 Jahren stand Herbert Blomstedt auf der Bühne. Viele Ensembles haben den schwedischen Dirigenten im Laufe der Jahre zum Ehrendirigenten ernannt. Darunter das San Francisco Symphony Orchestra, die Bamberger Symphoniker, die Wiener Philharmoniker sowie das NHK Symphony Orchestra in Tokio.
Blomstedt wurde am 11. Juli 1927 als Sohn schwedischer Eltern in den USA geboren. Der Vater war ein adventistischer Pastor, seine Mutter Pianistin. In seiner Anfangszeit arbeitete er als Chefdirigent bedeutender skandinavischer Orchester.

Rechtsradikale hatten in Chemnitz randaliert und regelrecht Jagd auf Migranten gemacht.

title: Яблука залишаться свіжими до весни. Сім помилок під час зберігання, які можуть зіпсувати весь урожай
content_c:
Яблука залишаться свіжими до весни. Сім помилок під час зберігання, які можуть зіпсувати весь урожай
Сім помилок, через які яблука швидко псуються (Фото: ignartonosbg/pixabay)
Зберегти яблука свіжими до весни цілком реально, якщо правильно організувати їхнє зберігання. Однак кілька поширених помилок можуть призвести до того, що вже за кілька тижнів плоди стануть м’якими, втратять соковитість і почнуть гнити.
За умови дотримання необхідних вимог яблука можуть зберігати свіжість щонайменше два місяці. Водночас фахівці американських університетів зазначають, що окремі сорти можуть зберігатися від трьох до восьми місяців, пише Kerteszkedj .
Сім помилок, через які яблука швидко псуються
1. Зберігання в теплі. Залишати яблука на кухонному столі або у вазі з фруктами — не найкраща ідея. За даними Університету штату Айова, за температури +10°C вони псуються у два-три рази швидше, ніж за температури, близької до нуля. Оптимальні умови — від 0 до +4°C. Для зберігання підійдуть холодильник, прохолодний льох або комора.
2. Занадто сухе повітря. Яблукам потрібна вологість близько 90−95%. У сухому приміщенні плоди швидко втрачають вологу, зморщуються і стають пухкими. Зберегти свіжість у холодильнику допоможуть перфоровані поліетиленові пакети, які утримують вологу та забезпечують вентиляцію.
3. Пошкоджені плоди в спільному ящику. Яблука з вм’ятинами, тріщинами та іншими пошкодженнями можуть виділяти більше етилену — газу, що прискорює дозрівання фруктів. Тому перед закладанням на зберігання врожай слід перебрати, а пошкоджені плоди використати найпершими. Раз на тиждень варто перевіряти запаси й видаляти плоди з ознаками псування.
4. Сусідство з овочами. Не рекомендується зберігати яблука поруч із картоплею та іншими овочами. Етилен, що вони виділяють, може прискорювати псування деяких продуктів. Крім того, фрукти здатні вбирати сторонні запахи. Фахівці Університету Пердью радять відводити для яблук окреме місце.
5. Миття перед зберіганням. На поверхні яблук є природний восковий шар, що допомагає утримувати вологу. Ретельне миття перед закладанням на зберігання може пошкодити цей захисний шар і скоротити термін збереження свіжості. Тому плоди краще мити безпосередньо перед вживанням.
6. Вплив морозу. Хоча яблукам потрібна прохолода, від'ємні температури можуть їм зашкодити. Приблизно за температури −1,5°C плоди починають замерзати, а після відтавання швидко псуються. Якщо врожай зберігається в неопалюваному приміщенні, важливо контролювати температуру та захищати ящики від сильних морозів.
7. Невідповідний сорт. Не всі яблука однаково добре переносять тривале зберігання. Щільні плоди з міцною шкіркою зазвичай зберігаються довше, ніж м’які осінні сорти. Серед сортів, придатних для зимових запасів, фахівці називають Granny Smith, Fuji, Rome та Idared. Останній за належних умов може зберігати свіжість аж до весни.
Як подовжити термін зберігання яблук
Фахівці рекомендують розміщувати плоди в ящиках вільно, уникаючи сильного тиску одне на одного. Для додаткового захисту їх можна розділити папером або картонними перегородками.
Якщо яблука вже стали м’якими, але не мають ознак гнилі чи плісняви, їх можна використовувати для приготування компотів, пюре, випічки або запікання зі спеціями.
Головна умова тривалого зберігання — стабільна прохолодна температура, достатня вологість і регулярна перевірка врожаю.

Підготовка до переговорів в Абу-Дабі та нова допомога для України: головні новини ночі 6 листопада 2026 року
ТСН.ua пропонує дізнатися головні події ночі.
ТСН.ua пропонує дізнатися головні події за ніч проти 6 листопада 2026 року:

title: «Это вообще абсурд»: в НАБУ рассказали, как «Альфа» защищала генерала СБУ
content_c:
Во время обыска у генерала Службы безопасности Украины к его дому были стянуты вооруженные бойцы «Альфы», а сам генерал молотком разбил два телефона и жесткий диск. Ранее в Национальном антикоррупционном бюро Украины сообщили, что высокопоставленный чиновник СБУ угрожал детективам оружием. По версии бюро, спецназовцы собирались вывезти генерала. Об этом рассказал руководитель отдела детективов НАБУ Александр Абакумов.
Детективы НАБУ прибыли на обыск по постановлению следственного судьи. В целях безопасности бюро привлекло небольшую группу из управления специальных операций: четырех или пятерых сотрудников. Когда они начали заходить на территорию домовладения, оказалось, что там находятся вооруженные люди. Один из спецназовцев хотел перелезть через забор, чтобы открыть калитку. В этот момент на него навели оружие с лазерным целеуказателем.
Вероятно, это было спецподразделение СБУ «Альфа», которое находилось в доме вместе с генералом. В окнах стояли как минимум двое людей с автоматами, а сам генерал держал пистолет в окне второго этажа. Абакумов через громкоговоритель представился, показал удостоверение и постановление и попросил не создавать опасную ситуацию. Люди на контакт не пошли. Вместо этого генерал выбежал на балкон и начал разбивать телефоны молотком. Затем он спрятался в доме. Вероятно, генерал пытался уничтожить или спрятать другие вещи, которые интересовали следствие.
Далее начались переговоры. Через 15–20 минут приехали сотрудники внутренней безопасности и адвокаты. С адвокатами удалось договориться о порядке проведения следственного действия. Тем временем к дому начали подъезжать вооруженные сотрудники СБУ из спецподразделения «Альфа»: сначала один микроавтобус, затем второй, а впоследствии еще одна машина. Абакумов подходил к каждому микроавтобусу и объяснял, что детективы не представляют угрозы, а попытка отбить человека штурмом станет правонарушением. Одни приезжие вели себя адекватно, другие — нет.
Спецподразделение, которое должно было содействовать следственным действиям, привлекли для того, чтобы защитить высокопоставленного чиновника от детективов. «Это вообще абсурдно», — подчеркнул Абакумов. По его мнению, изначально планировали силой забрать генерала и вывезти его из дома. Когда ситуация получила огласку, в НАБУ начали предупреждать, что она может перерасти в вооруженное противостояние. Бюро не намеревалось применять оружие, но если бы против детективов применили оружие, спецназовцы бюро ответили бы. Самым опасным был первый час. Затем ситуация как-то замерла.
Руководитель СБУ Александр Поклад 4 ноября уволил двух высокопоставленных сотрудников службы, фигурирующих в расследовании НАБУ в рамках операции «Карфаген». В тот же день бюро и САП сообщили о разоблачении еще одной преступной организации. Ее участники систематически платили высокопоставленным сотрудникам правоохранительных органов за беспрепятственную работу мошеннических колл-центров, продажу наркотиков, производство контрафактных сигарет и поддельной валюты. По данным НАБУ, стандартная плата составляла 7 тыс. долларов в месяц с одного колл-центра. Участники организации координировали не менее 52 колл-центров.
О том, как дело Осипова может вывести НАБУ на уголовно-клановую систему в силовом блоке, в статье «Вырождение власти. Как Зеленский достиг своего потолка, а система государственного управления — дна» пишет редактор отдела внутренней политики ZN.UA Инна Ведерникова.

title: Україна очікує переговорів в Абу-Дабі та розраховує на нову динаміку підтримки після виборів у США – Сибіга
content_c:
Україна розраховує на подальше посилення американської підтримки за підсумками проміжних виборів до Конгресу США та очікує проведення найближчими днями переговорів в Абу-Дабі (ОАЕ) щодо безпекових питань і можливого порядку денного зустрічі лідерів, заявив міністр закордонних справ України Андрій Сибіга у четвер.
"Безумовно, після проміжних виборів до Конгресу США ми очікуємо нової динаміки. Будь-які зміни завжди відкривають нові можливості. Тож так, ми розраховуємо на нову динаміку та нові кроки на підтримку України. Ми потрібні США, адже наша безпека невіддільна від безпеки Сполучених Штатів... Найближчими днями очікуємо переговорів в Абу-Дабі. Зосередимося на безпековому порядку денному, заходах зміцнення довіри та можливому порядку денному потенційної зустрічі Зеленського й Путіна", – сказав Сибіга на пресконференції в Бухаресті.
Глава зовнішньополітичного відомства наголосив на важливості американського лідерства у мирному процесі, яке має доповнюватися посиленою роллю Європи. За словами міністра, Київ використовує кожну нагоду для прискорення мирних зусиль та напрацював дієві пропозиції щодо подальшої залученості президента США Дональда Трампа до переговорного процесу.
Водночас у Російської Федерації наразі відсутні ознаки готовності до змістовного діалогу як на полі бою, так і на дипломатичному рівні, зазначив Сибіга.
"Ні на місцях, ні на полі бою ми не бачимо жодних ознак готовності Росії до серйозних переговорів. Досягти справедливого і всеосяжного миру можна лише тиском на Росію, санкціями, посиленням України та пакетом стримування для неї", – підсумував глава українського МЗС.

title: Melania Trump calls for lasting Ukraine truce as she hosts Russian and Ukrainian officials
content_c:
Melania Trump calls for lasting Ukraine truce as she hosts Russian and Ukrainian officials
- Published
US First Lady Melania Trump called for a "more enduring" ceasefire in Ukraine as she welcomed Russian and Ukrainian delegations at the White House following last week's truce in the southern region of Kherson.
Hundreds of residents of the Russian-occupied Ukrainian town of Oleshky facing starvation and constant bombardment were able to evacuate during a six-day ceasefire, which both Moscow and Kyiv credited Trump with brokering.
"The lives of innocent people must transcend the division of war. I hope Oleshky inspires greater peace," she said.
The unusual White House event saw senior Ukrainian and Russian officials meet away from the setting of official US-brokered peace talks they have been holding without success since last year.
The delegations were made up of Ukraine's human rights ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets and his Russian counterpart Yana Lantratova, as well as Ukrainian MP Davyd Arakhamia and Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev.
Melania Trump was credited by all for playing a key though unspecified role in the ceasefire, and all parties conveyed to her the gratitude of the Russian and Ukrainian presidents.
The US first lady said she had "reviewed demining plans, aerial images, assessed roadways, and discussed evacuation routes, hospital access, vehicles, and medical resources" during the truce.
"Last week in Oleshky and neighbouring areas of Kherson, people experienced the simple joys of life for the first time since 2022," Trump said. "They walked down familiar streets without fear of explosions."
She thanked both Volodymyr Zelensky and Vladimir Putin, making no reference to the origins of the war, which began when the Russian president launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, and which has caused thousands of civilian casualties and the displacement of millions.
Dmitriev, a businessman and Kremlin special envoy who has previously represented Moscow during peace talks with Ukraine, thanked Trump for "saving and touching so many lives".
"Let us continue making a humanitarian contribution together; this is within our power," Dmitriev said, before gifting Melania Trump a framed drawing by an 11-year-old Oleshky evacuee.
He also praised Trump for her work on reuniting children separated from their families by the war. These include children allegedly abducted by Russia.
Arakhamia, a Ukrainian MP who heads Zelensky's party in parliament who has also been part of the Ukrainian negotiating team, said the Oleshky ceasefire had constituted the "biggest de-escalation since 2022".
"We are creating a momentum where both sides are learning the… mechanics of how to actually keep the peace when the peace comes," he added.
He acknowledged that the "political track" of negotiations to end the conflict was "complex" but said Ukrainians were asking Melania Trump "to keep going and find new missions and de-escalate more."
At the end of the event, Trump handed Dmitriev and Arakhamia two letters to be hand-delivered to their respective presidents.
The White House later said Melania Trump had invited her guests to view two historic artifacts which she had "personally selected as powerful symbols of peace".
One was an 18th Century medicine chest which was removed from the White House when the British set it on fire in 1812. "Once adversaries, the United States and Great Britain ultimately established a strong alliance," the White House said.
The second artifact was a cup gifted in 1899 to the French ambassador in recognition of his efforts to bring the Spanish-American war to an end.
Melania Trump has generally remained discreet on foreign policy matters, and neither Moscow nor Kyiv have elaborated on the nature or extent of her involvement in coordinating the delicate ceasefire - the most enduring and widespread of the war so far.
A source who works in the local government of the Kherson region told the BBC that work on the Oleshky evacuation had been ongoing for almost a year.
However, the source said, "at a certain point other individuals became involved, seemingly after most of the groundwork had already been laid and subsequently began taking credit for the progress that had been made."
It was difficult to determine exactly who had played what role and at which stage of the process, the source acknowledged, adding that "those who had been directly involved in the negotiations for nearly a year were eventually prohibited from communicating publicly about the matter."
Speaking after the meeting in the White House had taken place, President Zelensky said the success of the Oleshky ceasefire "had proved a very simple thing: when Putin wants the fighting to stop, it stops."
"The same applies to our people who are held in Russian captivity. When Putin wants, they go home."
A source close to American officials shared a similar assessment, implying to the BBC that despite the outward praise, "the person who made [the ceasefire] possible, whether we like it or not, is essentially Putin."
"And this was done in order to pass the ball to [Donald] Trump... so that it would have some positive effect for his midterm elections."
There has been no change whatsoever in Russia's position, Ukrainian political analyst Dmytro Levus told the BBC.
Moscow "agreed to it because there was pressure from the American side... In doing so, the Russians confirmed Zelenskyy's words that, when necessary, it turns out Russia can quickly stop firing and even maintain that ceasefire."
As the frontline region of Kherson experienced its first six days of peace in several years, the rest of Ukraine continued to come under Russian attack.
This week, several drone and missile attacks killed and injured civilians across the country. On Monday alone, more than 40 people were killed in a single Russian strike on an aid distribution centre in the region of Zaporizhzhia. More are thought to still be buried under the rubble.
Additional reporting by Anastasiia Levchenko in Kyiv

content:
Melania Trump calls for lasting Ukraine truce as she hosts Russian and Ukrainian officials
- Published
US First Lady Melania Trump called for a "more enduring" ceasefire in Ukraine as she welcomed Russian and Ukrainian delegations at the White House following last week's truce in the southern region of Kherson.
Hundreds of residents of the Russian-occupied Ukrainian town of Oleshky facing starvation and constant bombardment were able to evacuate during a six-day ceasefire, which both Moscow and Kyiv credited Trump with brokering.
"The lives of innocent people must transcend the division of war. I hope Oleshky inspires greater peace," she said.
The unusual White House event saw senior Ukrainian and Russian officials meet away from the setting of official US-brokered peace talks they have been holding without success since last year.
The delegations were made up of Ukraine's human rights ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets and his Russian counterpart Yana Lantratova, as well as Ukrainian MP Davyd Arakhamia and Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev.
Melania Trump was credited by all for playing a key though unspecified role in the ceasefire, and all parties conveyed to her the gratitude of the Russian and Ukrainian presidents.
The US first lady said she had "reviewed demining plans, aerial images, assessed roadways, and discussed evacuation routes, hospital access, vehicles, and medical resources" during the truce.
"Last week in Oleshky and neighbouring areas of Kherson, people experienced the simple joys of life for the first time since 2022," Trump said. "They walked down familiar streets without fear of explosions."
She thanked both Volodymyr Zelensky and Vladimir Putin, making no reference to the origins of the war, which began when the Russian president launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, and which has caused thousands of civilian casualties and the displacement of millions.
Dmitriev, a businessman and Kremlin special envoy who has previously represented Moscow during peace talks with Ukraine, thanked Trump for "saving and touching so many lives".
"Let us continue making a humanitarian contribution together; this is within our power," Dmitriev said, before gifting Melania Trump a framed drawing by an 11-year-old Oleshky evacuee.
He also praised Trump for her work on reuniting children separated from their families by the war. These include children allegedly abducted by Russia.
Arakhamia, a Ukrainian MP who heads Zelensky's party in parliament who has also been part of the Ukrainian negotiating team, said the Oleshky ceasefire had constituted the "biggest de-escalation since 2022".
"We are creating a momentum where both sides are learning the… mechanics of how to actually keep the peace when the peace comes," he added.
He acknowledged that the "political track" of negotiations to end the conflict was "complex" but said Ukrainians were asking Melania Trump "to keep going and find new missions and de-escalate more."
At the end of the event, Trump handed Dmitriev and Arakhamia two letters to be hand-delivered to their respective presidents.
The White House later said Melania Trump had invited her guests to view two historic artifacts which she had "personally selected as powerful symbols of peace".
One was an 18th Century medicine chest which was removed from the White House when the British set it on fire in 1812. "Once adversaries, the United States and Great Britain ultimately established a strong alliance," the White House said.
The second artifact was a cup gifted in 1899 to the French ambassador in recognition of his efforts to bring the Spanish-American war to an end.
Melania Trump has generally remained discreet on foreign policy matters, and neither Moscow nor Kyiv have elaborated on the nature or extent of her involvement in coordinating the delicate ceasefire - the most enduring and widespread of the war so far.
A source who works in the local government of the Kherson region told the BBC that work on the Oleshky evacuation had been ongoing for almost a year.
However, the source said, "at a certain point other individuals became involved, seemingly after most of the groundwork had already been laid and subsequently began taking credit for the progress that had been made."
It was difficult to determine exactly who had played what role and at which stage of the process, the source acknowledged, adding that "those who had been directly involved in the negotiations for nearly a year were eventually prohibited from communicating publicly about the matter."
Speaking after the meeting in the White House had taken place, President Zelensky said the success of the Oleshky ceasefire "had proved a very simple thing: when Putin wants the fighting to stop, it stops."
"The same applies to our people who are held in Russian captivity. When Putin wants, they go home."
A source close to American officials shared a similar assessment, implying to the BBC that despite the outward praise, "the person who made [the ceasefire] possible, whether we like it or not, is essentially Putin."
"And this was done in order to pass the ball to [Donald] Trump... so that it would have some positive effect for his midterm elections."
There has been no change whatsoever in Russia's position, Ukrainian political analyst Dmytro Levus told the BBC.
Moscow "agreed to it because there was pressure from the American side... In doing so, the Russians confirmed Zelenskyy's words that, when necessary, it turns out Russia can quickly stop firing and even maintain that ceasefire."
As the frontline region of Kherson experienced its first six days of peace in several years, the rest of Ukraine continued to come under Russian attack.
This week, several drone and missile attacks killed and injured civilians across the country. On Monday alone, more than 40 people were killed in a single Russian strike on an aid distribution centre in the region of Zaporizhzhia. More are thought to still be buried under the rubble.
Additional reporting by Anastasiia Levchenko in Kyiv

title: Bomb threats disrupt dozens of flights across Europe, raising hybrid war fears
content_c:
Hoax bomb threats have disrupted at least 34 flights across Europe this week, with some forced to make emergency landings, as questions mount over an apparently coordinated effort to cause chaos for travellers.
At least 25 bomb threats affected flights on Thursday between Italy, Ireland, the UK, Spain, Bulgaria, Romania, Poland, Finland, Austria, Denmark, Belgium, Portugal, France, Greece, Serbia and Czechia.
The threats affected flights by Ryanair, Aer Lingus, Wizz Air, Finnair, easyJet, Aegean Airlines, Iberia, Sky Express, Air Serbia and LOT Polish Airlines. All landed safely. Searches of the planes found nothing suspicious.
In the UK, Heathrow, London’s principal airport, and Birmingham airport received threats overnight, but it was determined that they were hoaxes with the help of specialist investigators from the Metropolitan police’s aviation police command.
The Met said threats had been made against four aircraft departing from or arriving at Heathrow. A police spokesperson added that, after an assessment, “no security issues [were] identified”.
The day of hoaxes followed similar threats on Tuesday, when seven planes across Europe were searched or diverted after malicious alerts. On Monday a flight from the UK to Bulgaria was diverted after a threat that was apparently without substance.
Investigators said on Thursday there remained no evidence that the hoaxes were being orchestrated by a hostile terror group or state actor, such as Russia or Iran, although inquiries across Europe into the incidents continue.
The global airlines body Iata condemned the disruption and urged authorities to identify the origin of the threats. “Safety is the number one priority for the industry and we take all threats seriously,” said Nick Careen, Iata’s senior vice-president for operations, safety and security, in a statement.
The EU transport commissioner, Apostolos Tzitzikostas, said it was too early to know if the incidents were linked but that any threats against civilians were unacceptable.
Bomb threats emailed to airports in Rome and Sofia were signed “fighters of the Male State”, according to sources at Aeroporti di Roma, which manages the city’s two airports, and a text seen by Agence France-Presse.
Male State is a Russian far-right, ultranationalist and misogynistic movement founded in 2016 by Vladislav Pozdnyakov. On his Telegram channel Pozdnyakov, a prominent supporter of the war in Ukraine, did not comment on or claim responsibility for the bomb threats.
The emails reportedly read: “We, the fighters of the Male State, will make history with our actions today. Your feminist regime will remember this for ever. The explosion will occur in 60 minutes. Today, your skies will turn red.”
A Cork airport spokesperson confirmed to the Guardian that the airport had received an anonymous threat by phone on Thursday morning, causing a flight to be delayed. It was understood to be a Ryanair flight from London Stansted.
A separate Ryanair flight from Pescara in Italy to Brussels-Charleroi was inspected after the word “bomb” was discovered scrawled on the walls of its onboard toilet.
The affected flights had knock-on effects but were a tiny fraction of the 27,400 flights scheduled in Europe on Thursday, according to the European air traffic control agency, Eurocontrol.
The pilot of an Aer Lingus flight from Dublin to Rome that diverted to Évreux was being questioned by French authorities for initially refusing to land at a military base, according to French media reports.
The disruption followed cyber-attacks this week against supermarket refrigeration systems.
A Kremlin spokesperson said on Thursday it was “absurd” to blame Vladimir Putin’s administration for the fridge hacks. “We have such baseless accusations against our country, implicating it in everything,” Dmitry Peskov told reporters.
In Rome, Guido Crosetto, the Italian defence minister, said: “It seems to me that every day now, from refrigerators to blood supplies in France, to these fake alarms, there’s someone who has an interest in stoking tensions.”
Asked if he knew who was behind the hoaxes, he said: “It’s called ‘under-threshold warfare’ because it’s below the attribution threshold. It’s done that way on purpose, so no one can pin the blame.”
Many of the affected flights were operated by low-cost carriers but there was little discernible pattern surrounding the incidents.
Aviation experts say fake threats occur daily but that such a number of credible threats, even if malicious hoaxes, appears to point to coordinated action.
While getting a large explosive onboard should be ruled out by multiple layers of security and screening, the effects of any detonation would be multiplied for planes at typical cruising altitude of 35,000ft.
Diversions are expensive as well as highly disruptive, but airlines have little choice in the face of any remotely credible threat.
The ready availability of airline operations information on the internet means that any hoaxer now has a level of detail about the schedules, the type of plane and its technical specifications that would have eluded all but insiders decades ago.
Rhys Jones, an analyst at Osprey Flight Solutions, an aviation intelligence firm, said the confidence of airlines in European airport security should not mean any change to normal protocols after the hoaxes, but “one of the natural responses will be to see double-downed security, media coverage and public concern about travelling”.
He said the threats seemed linked but “a reasonably chaotic campaign with no particular region targeted”, and while they could weaken future security responses through the normalisation of threats, simply creating disruption could be regarded as a success by those carrying out the hoaxes.
Additional reporting by Pjotr Sauer in Amsterdam and Angela Giuffrida in Rome

title: Interest rate rise in midst of cost of living crisis will leave many incredulous
content_c:
An interest rate rise by the Bank of England to 4% is a big call when households are suffering from a second cost of living crisis in four years.
Many people will be incredulous when they hear of the decision to increase the cost of borrowing by 0.25 percentage points, looking around their neighbourhood for signs of a booming economy.
The official figures show the economy has proved resilient in response to the jump in oil and gas prices after the outbreak of war in Iran, but UK high streets are struggling and the underlying drivers of inflation are absent.
Most households are spending to stand still, whether it is on food, energy, holidays or leisure pursuits. Businesses are in much the same position. Like households, they have absorbed significant tax rises.
What the Bank’s policymakers believe is that despite all this, the energy price shock, being larger than first estimated, will surge through all parts of the economy, forcing up prices, encouraging a wave of wage demands that will, in turn, give inflation a second burst of life next year and the following year.
This analysis stands in contrast to the Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR), which acts as the Treasury’s independent forecaster. The OBR was clear in evidence to parliament on Wednesday that there was little impetus for strong wages growth.
The OBR said that, rather than economic growth next year of 1.6% and a rise in inflation to 4.9%, as the Bank expects, it believes the economy will expand by just 1% in 2027 and that the consumer prices index (CPI) will peak at just 3.75%. Inflation hit 3.5% in September, official figures showed.
The OBR’s chief economist, David Miles, said one of the main reasons for this assessment was the state of UK businesses, which he judged to be quite weak.
He said they had absorbed a large slice of the rise in energy and fuel costs, and their profit margins had plummeted on average as a result. Where once margins averaged 13% to 14%, the latest figures show they have fallen to 10% to 11%.
He said there would be little appetite to pay high wage settlements and the imperative would be to rebuild margins.
The wider economic situation is also very different from the previous crisis in 2022, when the country was coming out of the pandemic and dealing with the onset of the Ukraine war.
Back then, households were awash with lockdown savings that they wanted to spend, and firms were struggling to hire enough staff, leading to intense competition for workers and a spike in wages.
Today, savings are low and households bear the scars of four years of high inflation.
What sectors of the economy are making hay in 2026? Retailers and hospitality businesses are suffering, transport companies are battered by high costs and the charity sector is facing widespread financial difficulties. Vacancies are low, suggesting that firms have no need to employ more people.
Businesses in better-performing sectors such as banking and oil and gas also show little appetite for big wage increases. Banks are using artificial intelligence to shed staff.
The deputy director of the British Chambers of Commerce, David Bharier, said he was dismayed by the decision.
“So far, there is little sign of the wage-price spiral the Bank is looking to guard against. Unemployment is higher than in 2022, the labour market is looser and our research shows AI adoption accelerating rapidly – with some of the deepest users more likely to expect headcount reductions,” he said.
“After a budget which gave businesses little incentive to invest, and with borrowing costs already high, it is economic growth that will pay the premium.”
The Bank’s own survey of businesses and a separate report from its regional agents indicate “that wage and price expectations have moved little since September”.
It means Threadneedle Street policymakers judge that responses to their own business review will prove inaccurate and wages will jump.
The Bank judged that households’ and firms’ “attentiveness” to rising inflation was high and “there was a risk wage settlements would be higher than businesses expect”.
When the government says it is constrained by the bond markets from spending more to help consumers, there is a scenario looming in which ministers and the central bank, to meet their individual mandates, effectively crush the prospects for economic growth.
John Healey will say, as he did at the dispatch box last week, that he needs to restrict borrowing and adhere to his fiscal rules. Meanwhile, the bank will be busy making sure it cracks down on inflationary pressures it believes are on the way, even if policymakers cannot see them quite yet.

title: Paraguay: President Pena resigns amid bank crisis
content_c:
Paraguay: President Pena resigns amid bank crisis
November 5, 2026
Paraguayan President Santiago Pena resigned Thursday under mounting pressure over the collapse of digital lender Ueno, as lawmakers debated his removal from office.
The bank's accounts, also used to process pension payments, are frozen, leaving millions of customers unable to access their money. Ueno also held hundreds of millions of dollars in public funds.
Why did Pena face impeachment?
Pena's resignation followed the withdrawal of support by Congress President Basilio Nunez and ruling conservative Colorado Party leader Horacio Cartes.
Thirty-five opposition lawmakers and ruling-party dissidents had submitted impeachment articles in the 80-seat Chamber of Deputies, accusing Pena of conflicts of interest, misuse of pension funds and institutional cover-ups linked to Ueno.
Pena sold his shares in Ueno Holding, whose businesses include the bank, in April 2025. Lawmakers also cited two loans he received from Ueno as part of allegations of improper financial gain.
They alleged improper presidential interference in the Social Security Institute, known as IPS, and preferential treatment for Ueno. IPS manages pension and health care funds for most Paraguayan workers and held $355 million at the bank — about 9% of its investments, according to financial manager Gladys Vera.
The motion also questioned Pena's 2023 appointment of central bank chief Carlos Carvallo, who previously chaired Financiera Ueno. According to the document, the central bank approved the company's conversion into a bank just 83 days after his appointment.
What happened to Ueno Bank?
Ueno served about 2.94 million customers, roughly 60% of Paraguay's adult population.
As of last month, the bank said it held roughly $800 million in public-sector deposits — about a quarter of its total deposits — including money from the operators of Paraguay's giant hydroelectric dams.
Paraguay's central bank ordered a resolution or closure process Tuesday after finding that Ueno's solvency ratio had fallen below half the required minimum.
Ueno's app, card payments and transfers stopped working, while branches closed, leaving customers queuing outside unable to withdraw their savings.
Hundreds of employees of Ueno and other companies in its parent conglomerate protested outside the Labor Ministry Thursday, demanding unpaid wages and severance.
Retirees, depositors, students and workers had marched through Asuncion a day earlier, demanding Pena's impeachment and holding signs saying "Give us back our money."
What have authorities done?
Authorities detained eight senior executives, including founder Miguel Vazquez and bank president Juan Manuel Gustale. Prosecutors also charged 27 bank officials and business associates with offenses including breach of trust and attempted fraud.
Lawyers for several detainees said they needed time to review the allegations before commenting.
Pena had sought to reassure customers in a video message Wednesday, pledging legislation "that will return to every saver what they are entitled to as quickly as possible."
The crisis also forced him to cancel his attendance at the Ibero-American summit in Madrid.
Pena, a conservative economist, took office in August 2023 for a five-year term.
