Eine Zäsur war der Spätsommer 2023, als Aiwanger massiv in die Kritik geriet. Hintergrund war ein antisemitisches Flugblatt, das in seiner Schulzeit bei ihm gefunden worden war. Später sagte sein Bruder in einem Interview, er habe das Blatt verfasst. Das war kurz vor der Landtagswahl in Bayern. Die Regierungskoalition mit der CSU stand damals am Rand des Scheiterns. Aiwanger drohte der Rausschmiss. Dennoch feierte er bei der Wahl ein neues Rekordergebnis von 15,8 Prozent für die Freien Wähler.
Die gleichnamige Partei und die Vereinigungen der Freien Wähler in den Ländern und Kommunen sind strukturell zu trennen, insgesamt aber eng miteinander verwoben. Kommunal aktive Wählergemeinschaften sind über die jeweiligen Landesverbände in einem Bundesverband zusammengeschlossen - geschätzt haben diese Bündnisse insgesamt rund 280.000 Mitglieder.
Der als Verein eingetragene Bundesverband ist nicht zu verwechseln mit der Bundesvereinigung Freie Wähler, die 2009 zunächst als Bundeswählergruppe gegründet und 2010 in eine Bundesvereinigung umgewandelt wurde, um als Partei auch bei einer Bundestags- oder Europawahl antreten zu können. Diese Partei hatte laut ihrem Rechenschaftsbericht Ende 2024 etwa 8.800 Mitglieder. Aiwanger führte sowohl den Bundesverband als auch die Bundesvereinigung.
Die größten Erfolge feierte die Partei in Bayern, wo sie seit 2018 auch in der Regierung vertreten ist. Zwischenzeitlich waren Vertreter von Freien Wählergruppen auch in den Landtagen von Brandenburg und Rheinland-Pfalz vertreten. 2014 gewann die Partei Freie Wähler erstmals ein Mandat bei der Wahl zum Europäischen Parlament.

title: Литва виділила €12,3 мільйона на підтримку українців: на що спрямують кошти
content_c:
Литва виділила €12,3 мільйона на підтримку українців: на що спрямують кошти
Фінансування охоплює виплати дітям, компенсацію оренди житла та допомогу з оплатою комунальних послуг.
Уряд Литви схвалив виділення 12,3 мільйона євро на соціальну підтримку українців, які знайшли притулок у країні через повномасштабну війну Росії. Про це повідомляє Delfi.
Більшість цієї суми — близько 12,1 мільйона євро — призначена для відшкодування витрат за липень–вересень 2026 року. Майже 6,7 мільйона євро передбачено на виплати дітям, близько 1,8 мільйона — на соціальні виплати, 1,5 мільйона — на часткову компенсацію оренди житла.
Ще майже 1,1 мільйона євро спрямують на соціальну допомогу та покриття витрат на опалення й водопостачання.
Окремо 213 тисяч євро виділили на видатки за жовтень–листопад. Йдеться, зокрема, про опіку над неповнолітніми українцями, які прибули без супроводу, одноразові виплати на облаштування та компенсацію витрат на навчання дітей.
У Мінфіні Литви пояснили, що додаткове фінансування виділяють за фактичними зверненнями, оскільки під час підготовки бюджету точно визначити потреби було складно.
Іншим рішенням уряд виділив 30,1 мільйона євро на листопадові компенсації витрат із надання індивідуальної допомоги людям з інвалідністю. Загалом Міністерство соціального захисту та праці отримає понад 42,4 мільйона євро позикових коштів.
Нагадаємо, що Литва після прориву озброєних з Білорусі відправляє війська до кордонів Росії — перші деталі

title: Российская нефть подорожала до максимального уровня с 2014 года: сколько получил бюджет РФ
content_c:
Обострение ситуации вокруг Ирана и стремительный рост цен на российскую нефть привели к тому, что доходы бюджета РФ от нефти и газа достигли максимального уровня за 19 месяцев. Об этом пишет The Moscow Times.
По данным российского Минфина, в октябре бюджет получил 971,2 млрд рублей налогов от нефти и газа — на 82,6 млрд рублей больше, чем в октябре прошлого года (+9,3%), и на 518,8 млрд рублей больше, чем в сентябре.
Объем сырьевых доходов стал максимальным с апреля 2025 года. А поступления от ключевого налога на добычу полезных ископаемых (НДПИ) установили рекорд с февраля 2024 года. Они составили 1,122 трлн рублей и выросли на 39% по сравнению с сентябрем и почти вдвое по сравнению с октябрем прошлого года.
Еще 385,6 млрд рублей бюджет получил в виде налога на дополнительный доход (НДД), который уплачивается раз в квартал. Однако ещё больше — 415 млрд рублей — было возвращено нефтяным компаниям в виде субсидий для нефтеперерабатывающих заводов, которые в этом году более 100 раз подвергались атакам украинских дронов.
Аналитик Freedom Global Владимир Чернов объясняет: динамика цен на нефть поддерживает российский бюджет. В сентябре баррель российской нефти марки Urals продавался в среднем по цене $92, а в октябре его средняя стоимость достигла $101,46 за баррель — максимума с 2014 года.
«Рост стоимости нефти увеличивает нефтегазовые доходы и позволяет частично компенсировать недополученные поступления предыдущих месяцев», — отмечает Чернов.
По данным Минфина РФ, по итогам января–октября бюджет получил от нефти и газа 6,44 трлн рублей. По сравнению с аналогичным периодом прошлого года поступления сократились на 14%, однако этот разрыв сокращается: в сентябре, августе и июле спад достигал 17%, в июне — 23%, в мае — 30%.
Изначально Минфин РФ закладывал в бюджет на 2026 год 8,92 трлн рублей налоговых поступлений от нефти и газа, но в октябре снизил прогноз до 7,58 трлн рублей — нового минимума со времён пандемии COVID-19. В прошлом году нефтегазовые поступления сократились на 24%, до 8,48 трлн рублей, и стали самыми низкими за пять лет.
«Для нефтяных компаний дорогая нефть также означает увеличение выручки, хотя высокие налоги и транспортные расходы будут сдерживать рост прибыли. В то же время для российского бюджета гораздо важнее, как долго нефть будет оставаться дорогой, поскольку краткосрочный скачок цен не сможет полностью компенсировать сокращение нефтегазовых доходов за предыдущие периоды», — предупреждает Чернов.

title: У Словаччині затримано українця за підозрою у вбивстві співвітчизника в готелі: вони не є військовослужбовцями – МЗС
content_c:
Громадянин України загинув від ножових поранень у готелі в словацькому Тренчині, ще одного українця затримано за підозрою у вбивстві, розшукується ще один учасник інциденту, повідомила пресслужба українського Міністерства закордонних справ журналістам.
"У ніч на 5 листопада у готелі "SOG" у м. Тренчин внаслідок ножових поранень загинув громадянин України. За інформацією Регіонального управління поліції в Тренчині, чоловік отримав два колото-різані поранення в ділянки серця та живота і помер від отриманих травм та гострої внутрішньої кровотечі", – йдеться у повідомленні.
За підозрою у вчиненні цього злочину затримано іншого громадянина України. Ще один громадянин, який знаходився на місці інциденту, перебуває в розшуку, розповіли у відомстві. Регіональною кримінальною поліцією в Тренчині відкрито кримінальне провадження за фактом умисного вбивства.
"Всі згадані особи – цивільні. Двоє з них перебували в Словаччини у службовому відрядженні та не є військовослужбовцями Сил оборони України. Просимо не розповсюджувати недостовірну інформацію", – заявили у МЗС.
Зазначається, що посольство України в Словаччині встановило контакт із дружиною загиблого для сприяння у вирішенні питань щодо поховання. Справа перебуває на контролі установи.
Раніше начальник управління комунікацій командування Повітряних сил ЗСУ Юрій Ігнат заявив, що військовослужбовці Повітряних сил ЗСУ не причетні до бійки у м.Тренчин (Словаччина), внаслідок якої один чоловік помер від поранення,
"Ані пілоти, ані інший авіаційний персонал наразі не проходить навчання в Словаччині. Чимало українських військових проходять льотний вишкіл за кордоном, однак не у Словаччині", – сказав він у коментарі "Інтерфакс-Україна" у четвер ввечері.
Як повідомлялося, словацькі видання Nový Čas та Pluska писали, що у місті Тренчин в одному з готелів виник конфлікт між двома українськими військовими з авіапідрозділу, які проходять там навчання (за даними медіа, йдеться про представників Повітряних сил ЗСУ). Під час бійки 53-річний військовослужбовець завдав своєму ровеснику та колезі смертельного ножового поранення. Постраждалого намагалася врятувати бригада швидкої допомоги, проте він помер від отриманих травм під час транспортування до лікарні. Обставини та причини конфлікту наразі з'ясовуються, додали у ЗМІ.

title: A bitter end for Ronaldo - the icon who transformed Portugal
content_c:
A bitter end for Ronaldo - the icon who transformed Portugal
- Published
Cristiano Ronaldo's old rival Leo Messi left Argentina less than a month ago with a nation applauding him.
The Portugal legend has gone another way, and it was always going to be the case.
The 41-year-old announced his international retirement after 23 years but also after a fallout with coach Jorge Jesus which was resolved with a sanction of 30 days, that had already been served, and a fine of 255 euros.
It was the punishment imposed on the Portuguese striker for leaving the team's training camp without permission. Jesus kept him on the bench for one match and said he did not plan to start him in the next, so Ronaldo went home.
His last appearance came on 24 September against Wales. He ends his international career with 146 goals in 234 games.
A message went around Portugal with a big thank you for everything, calling Ronaldo a global ambassador and an inspiration to millions. Even so, the way it ended leaves a bit of a bitter taste.
Was he going to be named in the next squad? Possibly, as Jesus said the door was open and the decision was Ronaldo's. What is clear is that he was no longer an automatic starter, and Cristiano has never handled that well.
So is this another hissy fit? Partly, yes. He reacted the way he always has when a coach questions his place. But the label hides how much he adapted over the years.
Such a pattern appears with almost every man who sat on the Portuguese bench - there were clashes, but also communion with managers and team-mates that help explain this ending.
When a young Ronaldo first joined the squad, he arrived at camp with his baseball cap on backwards, enormous sunglasses and headphones turned up so loud they could be heard from a distance.
He would not take the cap off to eat among veterans like Luis Figo and Rui Costa. Luiz Felipe Scolari saw an extraordinary player who was immature and obsessed with showing off. He reprimanded him in public, then told him privately that if he changed his attitude, he would one day captain Portugal.
The first great disappointment came early, and it came at home. At 19, Ronaldo played in the final of Euro 2004 at the Estadio da Luz in Lisbon, in front of a country that had convinced itself the trophy was already on its way.
A single headed goal by Angelos Charisteas was enough for unfancied Greece to win it by surprise. When the final whistle went, Ronaldo could not hold back the tears, and the image of the teenager crying on his own pitch travelled everywhere.
It was a painful way to learn what a final costs, and it left him with a hunger that never really went away.
Figo owned the number 7 at the time, so Ronaldo had to have 17. Figo helped him settle but had no intention of making it easy. When he left the national team in 2006, the shirt and the team became Ronaldo's.
In September 2005, before a qualifier in Russia, Scolari and Figo went to his room to tell him his father had died. Scolari offered to send him home. Ronaldo chose to play, asked his team-mates to behave as normal, and spent time in the dressing room doing ball tricks.
That was his way to cope with the expected but still hugely hurtful passing of his alcoholic dad. He later called Scolari "father". That way the national team had become the place that held him together.
Things went sour with Carlos Queiroz. After the 2010 World Cup exit against Spain, asked to explain a poor performance, Ronaldo told journalists to ask the coach. His influence in the camp had grown so large it changed routines and habits, which explains why the coach felt undermined.
The sociologist Joao Nuno Coelho offers the best lens on how Portugal sees him. In his analysis, the national team became a representation of Portuguese identity and of the country's need to be seen internationally.
In years of economic hardship and a crisis of confidence, a team that won admiration abroad was important beyond football.
Ronaldo stood at the centre of that need and created contradictory feelings. Some Portuguese questioned his individualism and his ego, and not everyone saw themselves in his personality.
Coelho explains criticising him became more difficult as time went by. The country wanted to be proud of him and sometimes felt uneasy at the same time.
The former international Jorge Andrade told me some supporters preferred figures like Figo, Eusebio, Paulo Futre or Rui Costa. Even so, Portugal was proud to have him. And with the titles, the doubts eased.
Under Fernando Santos in 2016, he changed. He accepted playing as a centre forward next to Nani - he had never taken a coach's instructions so naturally.
After the opening draw with Iceland, he told Nani in private that he trusted Santos, and the dressing room began to see a real captain. After missing a penalty against Austria, he barely slept. Santos woke up and found him already awake.
At the training camp in Marcoussis, he took a fan's megaphone and told supporters Portugal had won nothing yet. He was enjoying the leadership role.
In the final in Paris, he left the pitch in tears, injured. He had not had the best tournament, with a muscle complaint that did not let him perform at his best.
Nani took the armband. At half-time Ronaldo pulled himself together to encourage his team-mates, and before extra time, still limping, he told Eder he would score.
And Eder did.
But the old instinct never fully disappeared. During extra-time, Ronaldo stood in the technical area giving orders until the fourth official sent him back. Other coaches I consulted found it excessive.
His greatest strength, the need to influence every result, also made limits hard to accept.
When he debuted in 2003, Portugal was still searching for its first major title. Some players mark an era, and others change a national team for good. He belongs to the second group.
That night in July 2016 gave Portugal its first European Championship.
Three years later he scored a hat-trick against Switzerland to put them into the first Nations League final, which Portugal won. In 2025 he lifted a second Nations League at an age when most players have retired.
No one has scored more goals for a national side, and no one has pulled on the Portugal shirt more times.
Under his influence, Portugal stopped being a gifted team and became one that arrives at every tournament expecting to contend, while a whole generation of players came through a dressing room where he decided what the standard was.
Coelho's point holds here as well: a small country found a way to be noticed, and for two decades he was its face.
After 2016 the question around him changed. Fewer asked whether he was selfish, and more asked whether Portugal depended on him too much.
In the World Cup in 2018, he scored three against Spain, including a free-kick after 45 attempts in major tournaments, and the team still went out to Uruguay.
After a difficult 2026 World Cup, much was made of him still starting up front when in fact statistically that was his best period.
Under Roberto Martinez, with 28 goals in 37 games, 0.756 per match, improves the 0.624 with Santos.
The federation has announced a special tribute to honour his contribution, and that is necessary as the exit has not left fans room for a celebration they want to be part of.
Not only they grew up with him, he took them to places they had not yet been.

title: Israel’s Herzog yet to decide on who should form government as Eisenkot secures significant backing
content_c:
Gadi Eisenkot, the main rival to Benjamin Netanyahu, secured endorsements on Thursday from a majority of lawmakers to try to form a government but Israel’s president, Isaac Herzog, said it was still unclear who could break the deadlock and that he would decide on Sunday which of the two men should try first.
Of the Knesset’s 120 elected lawmakers, 67 had endorsed Eisenkot through several days of talks with Herzog, while 46 endorsed Netanyahu. Herzog said on Thursday that while the “results of the consultations may appear clear”, there were “mutual vetoes between the blocs and within the blocs themselves” that make it difficult to say who has the best shot to form a government.
He said he would make a pick on Sunday, and that he would hold “personal talks with some of the party leaders” over the Israeli weekend, which runs Friday-Saturday.
A bitterly contested election last month, seen by many observers as one of the most consequential for Israel in many decades, ended with neither Netanyahu nor Eisenkot, a former military general and chief of staff, securing a clear pathway to power.
Netanyahu’s coalition lost its majority, dropping from 68 to 53 seats in the 120-seat Knesset. The Change bloc of Zionist parties led by Eisenkot has 48 seats, leaving parties representing Israeli Palestinians as potential kingmakers with a record 19 seats. The Joint List has 11, while the more conservative, Islamist Ra’am has eight.
In Israel’s political system, the otherwise largely ceremonial president decides which candidate has the best initial chance of building a stable coalition to rule.
Both Arab-majority parties reported backing Eisenkot, according to Haaretz. United Torah Judaism, though often aligned with Netanyahu, did not endorse either man.
Turnout among Arab Israelis – Palestinians with Israeli citizenship, who constitute 20% of the population – more than doubled to about 80%, transforming the political landscape. Palestinians in the occupied West Bank and Gaza had no vote.
The leader of Israel’s main Palestinian coalition has admitted to “disagreements with Eisenkot on many issues” but said on Thursday that Palestinian voters wanted change after facing intensified racism, discrimination, crime and exclusion under the current coalition.
“We are not choosing between good and better but between what we see as bad and even worse,” Yousef Jabareen said, according to Israeli media.
Last month, Jabareen told the Guardian that the first demand of Arab Israeli voters was to get rid of the Netanyahu government, and in particular its most extreme members, Itamar Ben-Gvir, the national security minister, and Bezalel Smotrich, the finance minister.
Eisenkot has also put conditions on any potential coalition with Arab parties: they have to recognise that Israel is a Jewish state, accept compulsory national service – either civil or military – and denounce Hamas as a terrorist organisation.
Jabareen and the Joint List have suggested they would support an opposition from the outside with tactical voting in the Knesset. Ra’am has said it would join a new government led by Eisenkot.
Herzog, who met delegations from the Palestinian Israeli parties and other small parties, has called on all to help avert another round of elections.
“Any reasonable person need only look at the security and diplomatic challenges before us, at the changing region around us, and remember the issues tearing us apart from within, to understand that an immense responsibility rests upon us,” Herzog said.
Netanyahu remains prime minister in a caretaker government until a new coalition is formed or there is another election, which must be held if no candidate succeeds.
Though the 77-year-old political veteran did better than expected in the vote and his Likud party won the most seats, his nationalist-religious coalition, the most rightwing government in Israel’s history, lost its governing majority.
Netanyahu, at risk of losing power, has seized on an investigation by election officials into possible vote tampering to cast doubt on the results, accusing Israeli Palestinian-led parties of stealing the vote. Critics accuse Netanyahu and his partners of trying to undermine the results, which he denies.
Israel’s Central Election Committee said on Wednesday that the election’s integrity had not been compromised. The head of the committee, the supreme court justice Noam Sohlberg, has called on the country’s elected officials to protect public trust.
“This is a real danger. One of the foundations of democracy is the peaceful transfer of power,” Sohlberg told Herzog at his residence on Wednesday. He said high voter turnout, including among the Arab minority, was a blessing.
Netanyahu’s allies on the far right, including Ben-Gvir, have called for the immediate arrest and interrogation of Arab party leaders.

title: What does Trump's midterm elections loss mean for strained US-India ties?
content_c:
What does Trump's midterm loss mean for India-US ties?
November 5, 2026
With the US Democrats scoring a resounding midterm victory and taking control of both chambers of Congress, the Republican administration led by Donald Trump is set for a new level of scrutiny until the end of Trump's term.
Trump is likely to face pushback on his controversial foreign policy, which saw the US alienate most of its allies and get entangled in yet another unpopular war in the Middle East. At the same time, the Trump administration has also taken a slew of less conspicuous but still highly controversial moves on the global stage, including a series of confrontations with India.
The ties between New Delhi and Washington are still strained by a stalled trade agreement, restrictions on immigration, and disagreement over India buying Russian oil and weapons, despite the US granting an oil ban waiver in March 2026 and Trump waving some of the Russia sanctions in October.
And while the new US Congress can choose to pressure Trump over issues such as tariffs and immigration, the president still wields significant authority on foreign policy.
Congress likely to look into Trump's trade restrictions
The immediate test for Trump's India policy is trade. India and the US have yet to formalize the interim framework discussed by Trump and Prime Minister Narendra Modi in February, with the two nations still at odds over market access and other trade commitments.
Shanthie Mariet D'Souza, founder of the Mantraya Institute of Strategic Studies, expects the new Congress to apply "increased scrutiny of protectionist measures" pushed by the Trump administration.
The US lawmakers could push for "stronger trade oversight and clearer standards for environmental and labor issues," she told DW.
For India, whose largest export market is the US, this could offer some breathing room.
She also emphasized that "the fundamental pillars of the India-US strategic partnership are expected to remain strong" and "the long-term goal of deepening economic ties is likely to continue."
'The president is not rational'
Immigration presents a different challenge. The administration's tightening of H-1B visa rules, including imposing a $100,000 (€88,761) payment for certain new petitions, has alarmed Indian professionals and tech companies that rely on the visa program to secure jobs in the US.
A Democratic majority could increase scrutiny on that issue as well, but would not automatically reverse measures introduced by Trump's executive action.
"Both parties have bigger issues to grapple with," said Rajkrishna Iyer, a California-licensed immigration lawyer. "For the last 25-plus years, Congress has done nothing for immigration," he added.
Iyer believes that legal immigration itself is not a major priority for voters. Nevertheless, he sees the midterms' result as a message to Trump about his immigration policies.
"A rational president would not spend time imposing further restrictions on legal immigration. But as we know, the president is not rational," Iyer said.
The immigration lawyer believes that new, steep fee for some H-1B applications will be challenged in court.
"Most likely, the new rules will not come into effect. And if they do, federal courts are likely to strike them down because the fees are not reasonable," said Iyer.
While the executive branch of government can raise fees to reflect administrative costs and inflation, Iyer argued that charges of this magnitude could deter people from pursuing legal immigration. "Only Congress can pass such legislation."
US still wants less dependence on Russia
The new balance of power in Washington could also trigger a new geopolitical reshuffle and a change of course on Russia. However, it is unclear if the Democrat-dominated Congress will force any changes in the dispute between New Delhi and Washington over India's purchasing Russian energy. During a congressional vote on Russian sanctions in September, a substantial number of Democrats joined Republican lawmakers to endorse trade restrictions against Moscow.
"Regarding Russian oil, the administration is likely to maintain its preference for reducing dependence on Moscow, but it will approach this issue with diplomatic caution to avoid straining relations with New Delhi," D'Souza said.
India angry over US supplying Pakistan with weapons
The war in Iran adds another dimension. Any new escalation could affect energy exports from the Middle East and make India more vulnerable due to its need for high oil imports.
But Navtej Sarna, a former Indian ambassador to the US and Israel, urged cautions when discussing the future of US policy in the Middle East.
"It may be facile to try and parse these results for their immediate impact on specific areas of foreign policy. Much will depend on how Trump reacts," Sarna told DW.
At the same time, Sarna expects Washington to become "a more contested place," with greater congressional pushback on issues that divide India and the US.
"If that injects some balance and stability and restores institutional linkages it's good for the long-term future of our relationship," he added.
Security cooperation is another stumbling block. New Delhi is still by far the biggest buyer of Russia's arms exports, which irritates Washington. At the same time, India has objected to US supplying weapons to Pakistan, including the $686 million sale of advanced military tech for Pakistan's F-16 jets.
"Washington's military support for Pakistan remains a complex issue. However, ongoing regional adjustments and US concerns about stability in the region will probably prevent any significant policy changes," said D'Souza.
Trump could 'double down' on New Delhi policy
The broader question is whether the election produces a more predictable Washington or a more confrontational Donald Trump.
A weakened president could be more inclined to seek compromises at home. But Trump could also respond to congressional resistance by taking a harder line elsewhere.
"We hope the electoral setback will prompt Trump to undertake a more considered review of his earlier actions," Amitabh Mattoo, dean of the School of International Studies at Jawaharlal Nehru University, told DW.
But he also warns that it too early to assess the implications for India-US relations.
"Rather than moderating his approach, the president could double down and adopt an even harder line towards New Delhi if he comes to believe that Indians, particularly sections of the diaspora, played a role, directly or indirectly, in his party's defeat."
Business as usual for US and India?
Harsh Pant of the Observer Research said that the US president retains considerable leverage over foreign policy despite the Republican setback, and that the India-US partnership has traditionally enjoyed bipartisan support.
"I don't think India will be one of those issues" on which the White House and Congress are likely to clash, Pant told DW.
But the experience of the past two years, he argues, reinforces the need for India to reduce its dependence on any single partner.
"The need for diversification of partnerships, the need to be self-reliant in certain critical sectors, the need to have alternative supply chains — all of those issues remain where they are. The US midterms do not really change the calculus," he said.
description: Donald Trump's electoral setback might give New Delhi and Washington space to reset relations, but there is no guarantee that the US will actually change its approach to India.

"Most likely, the new rules will not come into effect. And if they do, federal courts are likely to strike them down because the fees are not reasonable," said Iyer.
While the executive branch of government can raise fees to reflect administrative costs and inflation, Iyer argued that charges of this magnitude could deter people from pursuing legal immigration. "Only Congress can pass such legislation."
US still wants less dependence on Russia
The new balance of power in Washington could also trigger a new geopolitical reshuffle and a change of course on Russia. However, it is unclear if the Democrat-dominated Congress will force any changes in the dispute between New Delhi and Washington over India's purchasing Russian energy. During a congressional vote on Russian sanctions in September, a substantial number of Democrats joined Republican lawmakers to endorse trade restrictions against Moscow.
"Regarding Russian oil, the administration is likely to maintain its preference for reducing dependence on Moscow, but it will approach this issue with diplomatic caution to avoid straining relations with New Delhi," D'Souza said.
India angry over US supplying Pakistan with weapons
The war in Iran adds another dimension. Any new escalation could affect energy exports from the Middle East and make India more vulnerable due to its need for high oil imports.
But Navtej Sarna, a former Indian ambassador to the US and Israel, urged cautions when discussing the future of US policy in the Middle East.
"It may be facile to try and parse these results for their immediate impact on specific areas of foreign policy. Much will depend on how Trump reacts," Sarna told DW.
At the same time, Sarna expects Washington to become "a more contested place," with greater congressional pushback on issues that divide India and the US.
"If that injects some balance and stability and restores institutional linkages it's good for the long-term future of our relationship," he added.
Security cooperation is another stumbling block. New Delhi is still by far the biggest buyer of Russia's arms exports, which irritates Washington. At the same time, India has objected to US supplying weapons to Pakistan, including the $686 million sale of advanced military tech for Pakistan's F-16 jets.
"Washington's military support for Pakistan remains a complex issue. However, ongoing regional adjustments and US concerns about stability in the region will probably prevent any significant policy changes," said D'Souza.
Trump could 'double down' on New Delhi policy
The broader question is whether the election produces a more predictable Washington or a more confrontational Donald Trump.
A weakened president could be more inclined to seek compromises at home. But Trump could also respond to congressional resistance by taking a harder line elsewhere.
"We hope the electoral setback will prompt Trump to undertake a more considered review of his earlier actions," Amitabh Mattoo, dean of the School of International Studies at Jawaharlal Nehru University, told DW.
But he also warns that it too early to assess the implications for India-US relations.
"Rather than moderating his approach, the president could double down and adopt an even harder line towards New Delhi if he comes to believe that Indians, particularly sections of the diaspora, played a role, directly or indirectly, in his party's defeat."
Business as usual for US and India?
Harsh Pant of the Observer Research said that the US president retains considerable leverage over foreign policy despite the Republican setback, and that the India-US partnership has traditionally enjoyed bipartisan support.
"I don't think India will be one of those issues" on which the White House and Congress are likely to clash, Pant told DW.
But the experience of the past two years, he argues, reinforces the need for India to reduce its dependence on any single partner.
"The need for diversification of partnerships, the need to be self-reliant in certain critical sectors, the need to have alternative supply chains — all of those issues remain where they are. The US midterms do not really change the calculus," he said.

title: Midterms-Siege der Demokraten: Furcht vor KI-Regulierung lässt US-Tech-Aktien einbrechen
content_c:
Midtermserfolg der Demokraten Furcht vor KI-Regulierung lässt US-Techaktien einbrechen
Die Sorge vor einer stärkeren Regulierung in der KI-Branche hat am US-Aktienmarkt zu einem Ausverkauf bei Technologiewerten geführt. Zwei Tage nach den Wahlerfolgen der Demokraten bei den Midterms brachen insbesondere die Papiere aus dem Umfeld der Chipbranche ein, die bis in die jüngste Vergangenheit als größte Profiteure des Höhenfluges von KI gegolten hatten.
Der Nasdaq 100 sackte um 6,36 Prozent auf 26.629,81 Punkte ab und fiel auf das Niveau von April zurück. Damit verschwanden 2,3 Billionen Dollar an Marktwert; allerdings war der Tech-Index auch seit Anfang 2023 rasant gestiegen und hatte damit sehr stark von der Hoffnung auf gute Geschäfte mit Künstlicher Intelligenz profitiert. Erst im Oktober hatte das Börsenbarometer ein Rekordhoch erreicht. Seit Jahresanfang hat er noch um 5,5 Prozent zugelegt.
Für den marktbreiten S&P 500 ging es am Donnerstag um 4,36 Prozent auf 7353,73 Zähler nach unten. Es ist der größte Tagesverlust seit April 2025. Der Leitindex Dow Jones Industrial fiel um 3,44 Prozent auf 51.523,06 Punkte. Hier liegt das Plus seit Jahresanfang noch bei 7,2 Prozent.
So verloren Aktien des Chipkonzerns Nvidia 9,3 Prozent. Noch heftiger erwischte es mit Seagate, Western Digital und Sandisk große Werte aus dem Speicherbereich, die um bis zu 22 Prozent einbrachen. Ihre Produkte sind für Rechenzentren unverzichtbar.
Rechenzentren in der Kritik
Bei den US-Kongresswahlen hatten die Demokraten die Mehrheit im Repräsentantenhaus und im Senat erobert. Techkonzerne müssen sich nun etwa auf mehr Gegenwind bei ihren riesigen Rechenzentren für KI einstellen. Kritiker der KI-Rechenzentren verweisen unter anderem auf deren hohen Strombedarf, der auch die Energiepreise für die Bevölkerung in die Höhe treiben könnte. Hinzu kommen Sorgen wegen Lärm, Luftverschmutzung und Wassermangel sowie die Befürchtung, dass durch die Rechenzentren nur wenige dauerhafte Jobs entstehen.
Die Demokraten gelten den Chancen von künstlicher Intelligenz gegenüber als skeptischer als die Republikaner, die sich eher für Deregulierung starkmachen. In Texas hat die designierte Gouverneurin Gina Hinojosa von den Demokraten bereits ein sofortiges Moratorium für den Bau von Rechenzentren gefordert.
Die Anteilscheine von Micron büßten 17,5 Prozent ein. Der Halbleiterkonzern habe seine Pläne für ein Speicherchip-Werk in Taiwan wegen eines drohenden langwierigen Tarifkonflikts vorerst auf Eis gelegt, berichtete die Nachrichtenagentur Bloomberg unter Berufung auf Insider. Dies wirft Fragen hinsichtlich der Zukunft eines wichtigen Produktionsstandorts für entscheidende KI-Komponenten auf.
Die Furcht vor einer insgesamt schärferen Regulierung verschreckte auch die Anleger von Aktien aus dem Firmenimperium des Tech-Milliardärs Elon Musk . So fielen die Papiere des Elektroautobauers Tesla um fast elf Prozent und die des Weltraum- und KI-Unternehmens SpaceX um neun Prozent.

In Deutschland schlossen sich die Titel des Chipkonzerns Infineon der turbulenten Lage an, indem sie mehr als zehn Prozent verloren. Aus dem Dax erwischte es mit Siemens Energy und Hochtief aber noch weitere Indexwerte sehr deutlich, in die ehemals hohe KI-Erwartungen eingepreist wurden. Der deutsche Leitindex hatte zwischenzeitlich einen Rekord aufgestellt, schloss aber 0,43 Prozent tiefer bei 26.325,01 Zählern, der MDax verlor 0,92 Prozent auf 30.891,56 Zähler.

title: Großangelegter TV-Streich sorgt in Dänemark für Skandal
content_c:
Debatte über Verantwortung von Medien TV-Experiment sorgt in Dänemark für Skandal
Ist es in Ordnung, wenn 150 Menschen über Monate einen Freund und Kollegen belügen, um am Ende aufzulösen, dass alles nur ein Spaß fürs Fernsehen war? In Dänemark wird heftig über ein TV-Format diskutiert.
Der dänische Comedian Rasmus Wallbridge sitzt in einem leeren Kinosaal. Er denkt, dass er jetzt vielleicht einen Trailer seines Spielfilms zu sehen bekommt, den er gerade produziert. Doch stattdessen sieht er auf der Leinwand, wie er über Monate reingelegt wurde: Besprechungen, die mit versteckter Kamera gefilmt wurden, Menschen, von denen er dachte, sie seien Geschäftspartner, geben sich als Schauspieler zu erkennen.
"Also hat es den Film nie gegeben?", fragt Wallbridge einen Kollegen, der neben ihm sitzt. Wer habe denn die Reise nach Litauen bezahlt, will er wissen. Der Fernsehsender TV2, antwortet der andere Mann - und führt weiter aus: "Alle, die wir getroffen haben, waren eingeweihte Schauspieler."
Belogen und versteckt gefilmt
Das Gesicht von Wallbridge erstarrt, er ist geschockt und fängt an, fast schon verzweifelt zu lachen. Erst in diesem Moment erfährt der junge Comedian, dass er über vier Monate lang belogen und mit versteckter Kamera gefilmt wurde.
Denn Wallbridge dachte, dass er von einer Produktionsfirma den Auftrag für seinen ersten großen Spielfilm bekommen hatte. Fast 150 Menschen waren eingeweiht in den Plan des Fernsehsenders TV2. Der hat eine sechsteilige Sendung produziert unter dem Namen "Alle lieben Rasmus".
Vernichtende Reaktionen auf TV-Format
Die Reaktionen in Dänemark darauf sind vernichtend: "Heftig, grenzüberschreitend, verantwortungslos", sagte der Psychologe Michael Baastrup Portz im Interview mit dem Sender DR. Dieser Streich könne für den Betroffenen schwerwiegende Folgen haben.
Die lange Dauer der Lüge und die Tatsache, dass so viele Menschen beteiligt waren, könne dazu führen, dass sich der Betroffene frage: Wie konnte das passieren? Daraus könnten Sorgen entstehen, die sich möglicherweise zu einer Depression entwickeln, so der Psychologe.
Mehrere der Eingeweihten, unter ihnen auch Prominente, entschuldigten sich inzwischen öffentlich beim Betroffenen. Nach heftiger Kritik entfernte TV2 das Programm aus seiner Online-Mediathek und kündigte eine interne Untersuchung an.
"Schwerwiegende Fehler gemacht"
Ulla Pors, Programmdirektorin von TV2, gibt zu, dass ihr Sender schwerwiegende Fehler gemacht habe. Die Sendung hätte niemals in Auftrag gegeben und ausgestrahlt werden dürfen, sagte sie.
Zunächst hatte der Sender noch versucht, das Format zu verteidigen. Doch nach und nach kamen neue Vorwürfe ans Licht. In der entscheidenden Auflösungsszene soll die Tonspur verändert worden sein, so dass unklar ist, wie Rasmus Wallbridge den Schwindel tatsächlich aufnahm.
Wallbridge hat sich inzwischen mit einem Post auf Instagram gemeldet. Er sei gerade nicht an einem Punkt, an dem er sich an der Diskussion beteiligen könne. An den Sender TV2 richtet er die Worte: Falls die Verantwortlichen ähnliche Programme geplant hätten, sollten sie das lieber bleiben lassen.
Kulturministerin schaltet sich ein
Sogar Dänemarks Kulturministerin Zenia Stampe schaltete sich in die Debatte ein. Das Format sei ein glasklarer Fehler. "Ich bin der Meinung, dass TV 2 seine Glaubwürdigkeit nur zurückgewinnen kann, wenn der Sender offenlegt, wie er verhindern will, dass so etwas nochmal passiert", so Stampe.
Rasmus Wallbridge hatte laut TV2 zunächst zugestimmt, dass das Programm gesendet werden darf. Trotzdem habe TV2 hier eine Grenze überschritten, meint Thomas Pallesen, Medienrechtler beim Sender DR. In Dänemark gebe es viele Freiheiten bei der Produktion von Unterhaltungssendungen - aber: "Man muss sich gleichzeitig bewusst sein, dass man Sendungen über echte Menschen macht, die danach ihr Leben weiterleben müssen", sagte Pallesen.
Was als großer Streich gedacht war, ist für TV2 zum PR-Desaster geworden. Der Fall zeigt, wie schnell ein Sender Vertrauen verspielen kann, wenn Unterhaltung auf Kosten von Menschen geht.

title: Додайте це до яєць перед смаженням: простий секрет ідеального сніданку
content_c:
Додайте це до яєць перед смаженням: простий секрет ідеального сніданку
Цей простий трюк змінить вашу яєчню назавжди. Експертка розкрила секрет.
Приготувати ідеальну яєчню на вихідні — завдання, яке не завжди дається з першої спроби. Адже страва часто виходить або надто рідкою, або «гумовою». Зробити сніданок ніжним і кремовим допоможе один простий інгредієнт.
Про це повідомило видання Express із посиланням на інтерв’ю кулінарки та ведучої програми Barefoot Contessa на Food Network Іни Гартен.
Секретним складником, який повністю змінює текстуру та додає страві італійського акценту, виявився сир рікота.
«Якщо ви готуєте їх на дуже слабкому вогні та додаєте рікотту, щоб надати їм кремовості та трохи текстури, це зовсім інша річ», — пояснила Іна Гартен.
Вона додала, що завдяки такому доповненню страва за консистенцією стає «більше схожою на заварний крем». Щоб досягти бажаного ефекту, кулінарка радить спочатку збити яйця, додати рікотту, а потім злегка збити суміш ще раз, залишивши дрібні видимі грудочки сиру. Готувати страву слід виключно на повільному вогні.
До базового рецепта з її книги «Просто, Іна» входять яйця, молоко, вершкове масло, оливкова олія та рікота. При подачі вона рекомендує додавати свіжу цибулю-шніт, пармезан і пластівці червоного перцю.
Змінити смак яєчні можна й за допомогою інших кулінарних прийомів. Заміна звичайного жиру на коричневе вершкове масло, качиний чи беконний жир, кунжутну олію або олію з чилі додає страві нових відтінків, як і кілька крапель трюфельної чи оливкової олії першого віджиму наприкінці приготування.
Виражені вершкові осередки утворюються, якщо за кілька секунд до зняття з плити додати козячий сир, фету, грюєр або таледжо.
Додаткової насиченості страві нададуть копчений лосось, хрустка панчетта чи обсмажені з чебрецем лісові гриби. Наостанок свіжа зелень на кшталт кропу, естрагону чи кервелю разом із пластівчастою сіллю, білим перцем, гострим медом або бальзамічним соусом забезпечать яскравий фінальний акцент.
Нагадаємо, через постійні атаки РФ на енергетичну інфраструктуру та об’єкти водопостачання України перед нами часто постає питання, що можна приготувати за таких умов. У матеріалі ТСН.ua зібрали рецепти збалансованих страв з простих і доступних продуктів.

«Якщо ви готуєте їх на дуже слабкому вогні та додаєте рікотту, щоб надати їм кремовості та трохи текстури, це зовсім інша річ», — пояснила Іна Гартен.
Вона додала, що завдяки такому доповненню страва за консистенцією стає «більше схожою на заварний крем». Щоб досягти бажаного ефекту, кулінарка радить спочатку збити яйця, додати рікотту, а потім злегка збити суміш ще раз, залишивши дрібні видимі грудочки сиру. Готувати страву слід виключно на повільному вогні.
До базового рецепта з її книги «Просто, Іна» входять яйця, молоко, вершкове масло, оливкова олія та рікота. При подачі вона рекомендує додавати свіжу цибулю-шніт, пармезан і пластівці червоного перцю.
Змінити смак яєчні можна й за допомогою інших кулінарних прийомів. Заміна звичайного жиру на коричневе вершкове масло, качиний чи беконний жир, кунжутну олію або олію з чилі додає страві нових відтінків, як і кілька крапель трюфельної чи оливкової олії першого віджиму наприкінці приготування.
Виражені вершкові осередки утворюються, якщо за кілька секунд до зняття з плити додати козячий сир, фету, грюєр або таледжо.
Додаткової насиченості страві нададуть копчений лосось, хрустка панчетта чи обсмажені з чебрецем лісові гриби. Наостанок свіжа зелень на кшталт кропу, естрагону чи кервелю разом із пластівчастою сіллю, білим перцем, гострим медом або бальзамічним соусом забезпечать яскравий фінальний акцент.
Нагадаємо, через постійні атаки РФ на енергетичну інфраструктуру та об’єкти водопостачання України перед нами часто постає питання, що можна приготувати за таких умов. У матеріалі ТСН.ua зібрали рецепти збалансованих страв з простих і доступних продуктів.

title: «За эти деньги Украина должна бороться»: Зеленский о приостановленной помощи США
content_c:
Украина не получила от США 16 млрд долларов помощи, предусмотренной предыдущими договоренностями. На промежуточных выборах победили демократы: с января они будут контролировать обе палаты американского Конгресса и смогут вынести на голосование вопрос о помощи Киеву. "Поднимать этот вопрос и бороться за эти деньги нужно", сообщил президент Украины Владимир Зеленский.
Украине необходимо быстро наладить диалог с учетом нового расклада сил в США и заручиться поддержкой обеих партий, которая уже существует. «Сейчас у нас могут появиться дополнительные шансы получить помощь из Соединенных Штатов Америки», — сказал президент.
Украина должна добиваться этого пакета помощи от США. Другого выхода, кроме как укреплять собственный потенциал, у страны нет, по крайней мере, пока продолжается война. «Мы благодарны за все, что было предоставлено, но как минимум за эти деньги Украина должна бороться», — добавил Зеленский.
Зеленский не уточнил, какие программы и решения входят в эту сумму, за какой период она была накоплена и какую часть в ней составляет военная помощь. По подсчетам Исследовательской службы Конгресса США, с февраля 2022 года по март 2026 года Соединенные Штаты обязались предоставить Украине вооружение и военные услуги на сумму 67,8 млрд долларов. В то же время полная стоимость помощи, которую Украина уже получила, может быть ниже. Ее не раскрыли публично, отметили в службе.
4 ноября Зеленский надеялся на увеличение американской помощи после победы демократов. По его словам, демократы четко заявляют о поддержке Украины и восстановлении связей между США и Европой.
Перед переговорами в Абу-Даби президент полтора часа обсуждал подготовку с представителями президента США Дональда Трампа Стивом Уиткоффом и Джаредом Кушнером. Киев поднял вопрос о ракетах-перехватчиках для систем Patriot. Кроме того, украинская сторона уже передала Вашингтону свои предложения по завершению войны.
Последствия победы демократов для политики США в отношении Украины анализирует в статье ZN.UA «Трамп проиграл Конгресс, но не власть: чего Украине ждать от США?» бывший заместитель министра иностранных дел и посол Украины в США Олег Шамшур.
description: Киев готовится к новым переговорам о поддержке в связи со сменой власти в Конгрессе.

title: Україна планує відновити саміти Центральноєвропейської ініціативи під час головування у 2027 році – Сибіга
content_c:
Міністр закордонних справ України Андрій Сибіга під час зустрічі з генеральним секретарем Центральноєвропейської ініціативи (ЦЄІ) Франко Даль Масом обговорив пріоритети українського головування в організації у 2027 році та плани провести саміт лідерів в Україні після багаторічної перерви, повідомило Міністерство зовнішніх справ України у четвер ввечері у Телеграм.
"Я поінформував про ситуацію в Україні, ескалацію російського терору та мирні зусилля. Подякував Генеральному секретарю за його принципову позицію та активну діяльність, а також за гуманітарну допомогу ЦЄІ... Ми зосереджені на відновленні формату самітів ЦЄІ після багаторічної перерви та проведенні такої зустрічі лідерів в Україні наступного року", – сказав Сибіга.
Під час переговорів сторони розглянули ключові напрями майбутнього головування України в організації, зокрема парламентський, регіональний, міністерський і молодіжний виміри, а також готовність Києва надати об'єднанню нового імпульсу. Крім того, глава українського МЗС запросив генерального секретаря ЦЄІ відвідати Україну у зручний для нього час.

title: Yemen’s president sacks ministers and officers in attempt to turn tide of war
content_c:
The UN-recognised government of Yemen has shaken up its political and military leadership in an attempt to regain territory lost to the Houthis in September and lift the four-week siege of Taiz, the country’s third largest city.
A counteroffensive launched on 5 October and aimed at liberating the entire country from Houthi control has failed amid fighting that has left thousands dead on both sides. The air superiority of the government’s ally Saudi Arabia – which has had to fend off near-daily Houthi attacks on its airports and military bases – has not translated into progress on the ground.
Reuters reported on Monday that Houthi forces were only about 37 miles (60km) from Aden, the nominal seat of the UN-recognised government.
A burst of government dismissals and appointments reflects military reverses and possibly a perceived need to be more sensitive to the demands of southern Yemenis.
Between 1967 and 1990, the country was divided in two, and there is a strong movement built around the banned Southern Transitional Council (STC) seeking to revert to that division, or create a more federated country.
The government has become dependent on southern troops to fend off Houthi advances, but these forces insist they will fight only to defend land inside former South Yemen.
Fresh claims were also aired this week that STC leaders were coerced by the Saudis into dissolving the organisation against their will. The growing criticism of Saudi Arabia from STC officials in the media reflects their confidence that if the north is lost to the Houthis, the Saudis will have to let the STC operate openly. Not all southern separatists support the STC, an organisation that overreached itself in January, making it easier for the Saudi leadership to defer decisions on the southern question.
Some of the most senior figures in the UN-backed government are largely based in hotels in Riyadh rather than operating permanently from inside Yemen and the government is dependent on Saudi money to pay salaries. Critics say the administration has become a “hotel government”.
Earlier this week, its ruling executive – the presidential leadership council – met for the first time in months in Riyadh, where it addressed the loss of swathes of territory to the Houthis along Yemen’s west coast. Since then, the fighting has moved into the mountains around Taiz.
In an attempt to rebalance the north-south divide in his government, President Rashad al-Alimi sacked the long-serving information minister, Muammar al-Eryani, replacing him with Prof Salem al-Awlaki, previously a minister for the civil service and a spokesperson for the STC from 2017 to 2019. Alimi chose two other southerners as ministers for local administration and the civil service and appointed new leaders for the civil aviation authority, the ports of Aden and the ministry of transport.
He also sacked Yusuf al-Sharaji, the military figure responsible for the Taiz front and Abu Bakr al-Jabouli, a brigadier responsible for the Tor al-Baha axis. Widespread accusations had been made about al-Sharaji’s failure to manage operations, resulting in the fall of several areas and districts to the Houthis.
The task of lifting the siege of Taiz and coordinating forces has been handed to Maj Gen Rashad al-Yousfi, a career officer.
Part of the difficulty is the tension between the different forces fighting on the government’s side. It has been claimed that Abu Zara’a, the leader of the Southern Giants, has fallen out with the Homeland Shield Forces, which are funded by Saudi Arabia and affiliated with Abdulrahman al-Lahji.
The Homeland Shield experienced heavy losses, leading al-Lahji to file an official report accusing Abu Zara’a of treason, and warning that the situation in Dhubab, close to the strategic Bab al-Mandab strait, had become extremely dangerous for the government. Repeated claims that control of the strait had been wrested back from the Houthis were contradicted by the evidence.

title: Pioneering Jewish academy opens in Germany
content_c:
Pioneering Jewish academy opens in Germany
November 5, 2026
The western city of Frankfurt was a very conscious choice of location for the new academy, which is the first of its kind in Germany. Frankfurt has traditionally been a hub of Jewish intellectual life — still one of the most important centers of Jewish life in Germany today alongside Berlin, Munich and Düsseldorf.
Less than a 10-minute walk from the city's biggest synagogue, the Jewish Academy is also within sight of the historic festival hall building on Frankfurt Trade Fair grounds where the Nazis herded Jewish men in 1938 and deported them to concentration camps.
It was also here that the Central Council of Jews in Germany was founded in 1950; Berlin serves as its headquarters today. Frankfurt is also home to the Central Welfare Board of Jews in Germany (ZWST) and a Jewish museum that opened in 1988.
Jewish thinkers have played a key role in Frankfurt's intellectual and academic history. The city's Jewish community contributed to the establishment of Goethe University in 1914.
Another important legacy is the Jewish Lehrhaus (house of study). Founded in 1920, it quickly gained prominence and is today associated with the philosopher Franz Rosenzweig (1886–1929). It was closed by the Nazis in 1938. The new academy sees itself in the tradition of Rosenzweig's Lehrhaus.
A place of education and dialogue
Speaking at the opening ceremony on Monday, Josef Schuster, president of the Central Council of Jews in Germany, stressed: "We must combat hatred with education, education and more education."
Schuster said the institute was a "milestone” that represented the "Jewish community's determination to call Germany home." At the same time, he emphasized: "Jewish life in Germany is under greater threat than it has been since the crime against humanity that was the Shoah."
German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier also underlined the need to reject antisemitism "outright and without reservation." He added that it must also be combated politically.
The federal president said the murder of six million Jews in the Holocaust had also targeted the Jewish world of learning and knowledge. He specifically honored Rosenzweig's legacy: "This place of knowledge and dialogue was a source of hope, something exciting and something new."
A bridge between tradition and modernity, as well as academia and the general public
The Jewish Academy combines traditional features of a 110-year-old turn-of-the-century German villa with a four-story modern structure, bringing together old and new, history and modernity.
"We see ourselves as a place where the past, present and future are all explored in equal measure," Sabena Donath, the institution's director, told DW.
Donath and her co-director, Doron Kiesel, view the academy as "a bridge between academia and the general public" and as "a home for scholars and a home for those who ask questions."
Donath said the aim was to put the focus on topics related to the philosophy of religion and ethics as well as on topical debates concerning contemporary Jewish life.
The program aims to reflect the many facets of Jewish life and the diverse forms of Judaism.
Kiesel told DW: "We want to show how Jews live today and how heterogeneous Jewish life is. And that it is completely wrong to speak of 'the' Jews or 'the' Jewish way of thinking."
Ahead of the opening, the president of the Central Council of Jews also named interfaith dialogue as one of the institution's topics, and, in an interview with the German newspaper, the Frankfurter Allgemeine, Schuster expressed the hope that the academy would bring into the public sphere "Jewish themes besides the topic of antisemitism and Jewish persecution.”
But these issues will also be on the agenda. "We have,” said Kiesel, "a problem in this country that antisemitism is concealed behind numerous topics, but keeps on resurfacing, sometimes more evidently, sometimes more subtly.”
The project grew out of an initiative from the former head of the Central Council Dieter Graumann, who encouraged the setting up of an educational department in 2012. Its work was shaped by the directors of the new institution.
Security measures push up price tab
A mezuzah — a small capsule containing verses from the Torah intended to serve as a reminder of God's commandments — is affixed to the entrance of the academy. Security measures are also an integral part of this new building.
"It is a bitter reality that Jewish institutions must be guarded," said Donath. The academy is being protected just as Jewish schools and synagogues must be protected. "For us, this is a sad reality of everyday life."
The construction costs of around €40 million ($45 million) — about half of which was covered by the Central Council of Jews and half by the federal and state governments — ended up being significantly higher than calculated at the groundbreaking in 2021, partly due to the structural security measures.
description: A Jewish academy has opened its doors in Frankfurt. The Central Council of Jews in Germany, the country’s leading Jewish umbrella group, set up the project to combat hate and promote dialogue and learning nationally.
content:
Pioneering Jewish academy opens in Germany
November 5, 2026
The western city of Frankfurt was a very conscious choice of location for the new academy, which is the first of its kind in Germany. Frankfurt has traditionally been a hub of Jewish intellectual life — still one of the most important centers of Jewish life in Germany today alongside Berlin, Munich and Düsseldorf.
Less than a 10-minute walk from the city's biggest synagogue, the Jewish Academy is also within sight of the historic festival hall building on Frankfurt Trade Fair grounds where the Nazis herded Jewish men in 1938 and deported them to concentration camps.
It was also here that the Central Council of Jews in Germany was founded in 1950; Berlin serves as its headquarters today. Frankfurt is also home to the Central Welfare Board of Jews in Germany (ZWST) and a Jewish museum that opened in 1988.
Jewish thinkers have played a key role in Frankfurt's intellectual and academic history. The city's Jewish community contributed to the establishment of Goethe University in 1914.
Another important legacy is the Jewish Lehrhaus (house of study). Founded in 1920, it quickly gained prominence and is today associated with the philosopher Franz Rosenzweig (1886–1929). It was closed by the Nazis in 1938. The new academy sees itself in the tradition of Rosenzweig's Lehrhaus.
A place of education and dialogue
Speaking at the opening ceremony on Monday, Josef Schuster, president of the Central Council of Jews in Germany, stressed: "We must combat hatred with education, education and more education."
Schuster said the institute was a "milestone” that represented the "Jewish community's determination to call Germany home." At the same time, he emphasized: "Jewish life in Germany is under greater threat than it has been since the crime against humanity that was the Shoah."
German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier also underlined the need to reject antisemitism "outright and without reservation." He added that it must also be combated politically.
The federal president said the murder of six million Jews in the Holocaust had also targeted the Jewish world of learning and knowledge. He specifically honored Rosenzweig's legacy: "This place of knowledge and dialogue was a source of hope, something exciting and something new."
A bridge between tradition and modernity, as well as academia and the general public
The Jewish Academy combines traditional features of a 110-year-old turn-of-the-century German villa with a four-story modern structure, bringing together old and new, history and modernity.
"We see ourselves as a place where the past, present and future are all explored in equal measure," Sabena Donath, the institution's director, told DW.
Donath and her co-director, Doron Kiesel, view the academy as "a bridge between academia and the general public" and as "a home for scholars and a home for those who ask questions."
Donath said the aim was to put the focus on topics related to the philosophy of religion and ethics as well as on topical debates concerning contemporary Jewish life.
The program aims to reflect the many facets of Jewish life and the diverse forms of Judaism.
Kiesel told DW: "We want to show how Jews live today and how heterogeneous Jewish life is. And that it is completely wrong to speak of 'the' Jews or 'the' Jewish way of thinking."
Ahead of the opening, the president of the Central Council of Jews also named interfaith dialogue as one of the institution's topics, and, in an interview with the German newspaper, the Frankfurter Allgemeine, Schuster expressed the hope that the academy would bring into the public sphere "Jewish themes besides the topic of antisemitism and Jewish persecution.”
But these issues will also be on the agenda. "We have,” said Kiesel, "a problem in this country that antisemitism is concealed behind numerous topics, but keeps on resurfacing, sometimes more evidently, sometimes more subtly.”
The project grew out of an initiative from the former head of the Central Council Dieter Graumann, who encouraged the setting up of an educational department in 2012. Its work was shaped by the directors of the new institution.
Security measures push up price tab
A mezuzah — a small capsule containing verses from the Torah intended to serve as a reminder of God's commandments — is affixed to the entrance of the academy. Security measures are also an integral part of this new building.
"It is a bitter reality that Jewish institutions must be guarded," said Donath. The academy is being protected just as Jewish schools and synagogues must be protected. "For us, this is a sad reality of everyday life."
The construction costs of around €40 million ($45 million) — about half of which was covered by the Central Council of Jews and half by the federal and state governments — ended up being significantly higher than calculated at the groundbreaking in 2021, partly due to the structural security measures.

title: Harmeet Dhillon: Trump-Vertraute tritt zurück
content_c:
Nach Pleite bei den Midterms Trump-Vertraute gibt Spitzenposition im Justizministerium auf
Sie galt als wichtige Mitstreiterin von US-Präsident Donald Trump, doch nun hat sie offenbar genug: Die Spitzenbeamtin Harmeet Dhillon aus dem Justizministerium räumt ihren Posten. US-Justizminister Todd Blanche bestätigte in einem Beitrag auf X , dass er Dhillons Rücktritt angenommen habe.
Damit ist Dhillon die erste ranghohe Trump-Vertraute, die ihren Hut nimmt, nachdem die Republikaner bei den Wahlen am Dienstag ihre Mehrheiten in beiden Kammern des US-Kongresses verloren haben. Der Nachrichtenagentur Reuters zufolge hatte Dhillon dem Weißen Haus bereits im Oktober mitgeteilt, nach den Midterms zurückzutreten. Unter Berufung auf zwei anonyme Quellen berichtet Reuters, sie sei frustriert über ausbleibende Beförderungen gewesen.
Dhillon hatte bisher die Abteilung für Bürgerrechte im Justizministerium geleitet und im Sinne Trumps umgekrempelt. Der Bereich war während der Bürgerrechtsbewegung des Landes zum Schutz der Rechte von Minderheiten geschaffen worden. Kritiker werfen ihr vor, diesen traditionellen Auftrag zugunsten konservativer Anliegen aufgegeben zu haben.
Sie habe dafür gesorgt, dass der Fokus nicht mehr auf die Bekämpfung von Diskriminierung ethnischer Minderheiten und die Untersuchung umstrittener Polizeipraktiken gelegt wurde, sondern auf Themen, die für Trump Priorität hätten. So verantwortete Dhillon etwa das harte Vorgehen gegen propalästinensische Demonstrationen an Universitäten nach Ausbruch des Gazakrieges.
Immer wieder legte sich Dhillon mit US-Universitäten wegen deren Aufnahmeregelungen an, die angeblich weiße Studierende benachteiligen würden. Gegen die Eliteuniversität Harvard klagte sie wegen der angeblichen Tolerierung von Antisemitismus. Die Klage wurde von einem Bundesrichter zurückgewiesen.
Der Biden-Regierung hatte Dhillon vorgeworfen, eine fehlgeleitete liberale Agenda zu verfolgen. In einem Interview mit dem konservativen Kommentator Glenn Beck sagte sie mit Blick auf ihre Abteilung: »Die Aufgabe hier ist es, die Bundesbürgerrechtsgesetze durchzusetzen – nicht die Woke-Ideologie.«
Lesen Sie hier , wie die ersten Republikaner auf Distanz zu Trump gehen – während die treuesten MAGA-Jünger weiter zum Präsidenten halten.

title: Bund und Eigentümerfamilien einigen sich auf Kaufpreis bei KNDS
content_c:
Deutsch-französischer Panzerbauer Bund steigt mit 50 Prozent bei KNDS ein
Die Bundesregierung übernimmt alle Anteile der Eigentümerfamilien am Panzerbauer KNDS. Damit sichert sich der Bund den Einfluss auf Schlüsseltechnologien - und gibt offenbar weniger Geld aus als geplant.
Die Bundesregierung hat sich mit der jetzigen Eigentümerfamilien grundsätzlich über einen Einstieg des Bundes beim deutsch-französischen Panzerbauer KNDS geeinigt. Das hat das ARD-Hauptstadtstudio aus Regierungskreisen erfahren.
Seit längerem versuchen die Familien des Panzerbauers aus München ihre Anteile an KNDS zu veräußern. Zunächst sollte dies über einen Börsengang geschehen, doch die Pläne wurden erst verschoben und im Herbst komplett abgesagt. Die Familien Braunbehrens und Bode halten über die Wegmann-Holding 50 Prozent an KNDS, die anderen 50 Prozent hält der französische Staat.
Man plane eine Beteiligung in gleicher Höhe wie Frankreich von 50 Prozent, um auf Augenhöhe mit dem Partner zu stehen, heißt es aus Regierungskreisen nun. Aus Vertraulichkeitsgründen könnten zu der erzielten Einigung keine Details genannt werden. Das Handelsblatt hatte als erstes über die Einigung berichtet, die noch im November unterschriftsreif sein soll. KNDS und die Familien äußerten sich nicht.
Kaufpreis unter 7,2 Milliarden Euro
Unklar ist, wie viel Geld der Bund auf den Tisch legen wird. Aus einer der Nachrichtenagentur Reuters vorliegenden Unterrichtung für den Haushaltsausschuss des Bundestages geht nur hervor, dass der Bund weniger als ursprünglich geplant bezahlen wird. Der Ausschuss hatte im Juni den Kauf für einen Preis von 7,2 Milliarden Euro für lediglich 40 Prozent bewilligt.
Das Bundeswirtschaftsministerium wollte eine Einigung noch nicht bestätigen, betonte aber die Bedeutung des "Leopard 2"- und "Boxer"-Herstellers für die Sicherheitsinteressen des Landes. Mit dem Einstieg bei KNDS wolle die Regierung den Schutz verteidigungsindustrieller Schlüsseltechnologie im Panzerbau sichern. Die Bundeswehr ist der größte Kunde von KNDS.
Zeitweise hatten die Eigentümerfamilien auch mit einem Verkauf an ausländische Investoren geliebäugelt - darunter das tschechische Rüstungsunternehmen Czechoslovak Group (CSG) und der US-amerikanische Private-Equity-Investor Warburg Pincus. Nun sollen die Familien einen Paketzuschlag erhalten haben sowie einen Anteil an der Dividende für 2026, die der Bund kassiert.
Neuer Versuch eines Börsengangs?
An den Börsenplänen, auf deren schnellstmögliche Umsetzung auch KNDS selbst pocht, hält die Bundesregierung gleichwohl fest. Mit Frankreich sei vereinbart worden, die jeweiligen Beteiligungen um zehn Prozent abzuschmelzen, hieß es. Für die Bundesregierung wäre das auch eine Möglichkeit, die Staatsbeteiligung zu reduzieren, wenn der Aktienkurs günstig ist.
KNDS entstand 2015 durch die Fusion von Krauss-Maffei Wegmann und dem französischen Unternehmen Nexter. Der Konzern beschäftigt gut 11.000 Menschen und erzielte im Geschäftsjahr 2025 einen Umsatz von 4,4 Milliarden Euro. Hauptsitz ist Amsterdam, die deutsche Zentrale sitzt in München. In Kassel betreibt KNDS drei Produktionsstandorte und einen Logistikstandort.

title: Росія ігнорує наказ зупинити війну: Мельник закликав ООН відреагувати
content_c:
Росія ігнорує наказ зупинити війну: Мельник закликав ООН відреагувати
Український дипломат нагадав про невиконані Росією накази Міжнародного суду ООН щодо війни та заборони Меджлісу в окупованому Криму.
Постійний представник України при ООН Андрій Мельник закликав Раду Безпеки та Генеральну Асамблею розглянути відмову Росії виконувати рішення Міжнародного суду ООН. Про це він заявив під час обговорення доповіді суду на засіданні Генасамблеї, повідомляє Укрінформ.
Дипломат наголосив, що Москва не виконала наказ від березня 2022 року про припинення воєнних дій проти України. Також Росія ігнорує наказ 2017 року про скасування заборони Меджлісу кримськотатарського народу в окупованому Криму.
«Сотні ракет і безпілотників – це єдина відповідь, яку ми чуємо щодня», — заявив Мельник.
Він нагадав про обов’язковість виконання рішень суду та закликав органи ООН відреагувати на дії Росії.
Під час засідання представниця РФ знову звинуватила Україну в нібито «геноциді» на Донбасі. У відповідь Мельник назвав Росію «чемпіоном з брехні» та заявив про неприйнятність погроз на адресу українського дипломата.
Нагадаємо, що раніше США запровадили санкції проти президентки МКС, яка видавала ордер на арешт Путіна

title: Срок действия соглашения по Starshield подходит к концу: Украина просит США о новых переговорах
content_c:
Украина стремится в срочном порядке начать переговоры с США о новом соглашении о доступе к спутниковой сети Starshield, поскольку действующий контракт истекает уже в 2027 году. Об этом сообщил временный поверенный в делах посольства Украины в Вашингтоне Денис Сеник, передает Reuters.
"Контракт на Starshield истекает в следующем году. И мы понимаем, что для переговоров о заключении нового контракта нужно время. Сейчас как раз тот момент. По сути, мы хотим получить ясность: сможем ли мы продолжить сотрудничество и какими будут условия", — рассказал журналистам Сеник.
Дипломат также сообщил, что власти Украины обращались с просьбой к президенту США Дональду Трампу, Пентагону и руководству SpaceX о снятии ограничений скорости Starshield, однако ответа так и не получили.
Ранее сообщалось, что демократы в Сенате США намерены провести расследование в отношении ограничений работы спутниковой системы Starshield в Украине.
Республиканский сенатор Том Тиллис обратился к генеральному инспектору Министерства обороны США с требованием начать расследование. Конгрессмен-республиканец Брайан Фицпатрик анонсировал слушания и сокращение финансирования ведомств, причастных к ограничениям.

title: Словаччина приєдналася до Міжнародної коаліції за повернення українських дітей – Сибіга
content_c:
Словаччина приєдналася до Міжнародної коаліції за повернення українських дітей і стала її 53-м учасником, повідомив міністр закордонних справ України Андрій Сибіга у четвер.
"Дякую Словаччині за приєднання до Міжнародної коаліції за повернення українських дітей як її 53-му учаснику. Кожен новий учасник посилює наші спільні зусилля задля повернення українських дітей на Батьківщину. Це також є потужним сигналом про те, що міжнародна спільнота не приймає і не толеруватиме незаконну депортацію та примусове переміщення Росією українських дітей", – повідомило Міністерства закордонних справ цитуючи Сибігу у телеграм-каналі.
Глава МЗС наголосив, що звільнення та репатріація примусово переміщених Росією дітей мають відбуватися вже зараз і залишатися обов'язковою складовою будь-яких зусиль із досягнення справедливого миру. Міністр додав, що Україна разом із міжнародними партнерами продовжить спільну роботу до повернення кожної дитини додому та притягнення до відповідальності всіх причетних до цих злочинів осіб.

title: Slashing number of police forces in England and Wales is only option, says Met chief
content_c:
Police are heading for failure unless the number of forces in England and Wales is slashed, with their ability to catch criminals collapsing and public confidence falling, Britain’s top officer will say on Friday.
The stark comments from Sir Mark Rowley, the commissioner of the Metropolitan police, come as some police leaders demand a radical package of reforms.
An official review ordered by the government has concluded that the number of police forces in England should be cut from 39 to as few as nine “super forces”, according to multiple sources.
The review, carried out by the former Met police commissioner Bernard Hogan-Howe, is yet to be published.
Sources say that under consideration is the establishment of nine regional forces, plus a single force for Wales, which would sit above more than 150 local policing units that would deliver most neighbourhood crime-fighting activities.
The axing of most of the 43 forces in England and Wales is seen as essential by the Hogan-Howe review and some police chiefs. Those chiefs, including Rowley, are concerned that the government may delay the most radical change to policing in seven decades.
Hogan-Howe’s review was completed in September and sent to the home secretary, Shabana Mahmood. Government sources say only that it will be published before Christmas, with a white paper due in the new year.
The delay is understood to be because of Andy Burnham’s devolution agenda and desire to “rewire” the British state and reform local government, including adding more mayors.
One police source said: “There are some concerns Andy Burnham may want to align the new police structures with mayors, which could mean 20 or more forces. That is not a radical enough change.”
Rowley will speak at an event in Manchester on Friday where he and other chiefs including Greater Manchester’s chief constable, Sir Stephen Watson, will press for a reduction in the number of forces.
The event’s title is “The cost of standing still is that criminals will win”. Some other chief constables have told the Guardian they are annoyed by the Met-organised event and are sceptical or do not support the big reduction down to nine forces.
Cutting the number of forces in England and Wales is the centrepiece of Mahmood’s radical changes to policing. Hogan-Howe’s report, multiple sources say, gives a range of how many larger forces there should be in the new policing landscape, from nine to 18.
Rowley will say in his speech that public confidence has already fallen and that positive outcomes – that is, crimes detected by officers that lead to a charge, caution, out of court settlement or no further action – “are now less than half what they were 12 years ago”.
According to extracts released before the speech, Rowley will say: “I believe this is a choice between the third greatest revolution in British policing or the inevitable decline and fewer bobbies on the beat.”
He will say the 43 forces in England and Wales should be cut to eight or 10, and add: “Policing has tried to keep up, made do as best it can to patch over our broken model … But the model is creaking. We have 43 overstretched forces trying to do too much with too little.”
Hogan-Howe believes the changes would free up policing to rapidly innovate as new crime types and threats emerge. The 43 forces model, overseen by 43 police and crime commissioners, is accused of being too slow and delivering a postcode lottery of varying service for crime victims.
Hogan-Howe came out publicly in favour of a reduction to nine forces 12 years ago.
The bigger forces would handle major crimes – such as murders and serious sexual violence – and public order, as well as expensive but essential back-office functions such as human resources, currently done by each of the 43 forces individually.
Above the regional forces would sit a new nationwide force called the National Police Service, which the government wants to be the home of counter-terrorism policing and serious and organised crime. The advert for a commissioner for the national force is expected to be issued early in the new year.
There is division among police leaders about the big reduction in forces. Some favour voluntary mergers, and the new white paper will allow the mass abolition of forces and creation of new ones to be enforced.
The changes could lead to a vast south-east England force stretching from the London borders to the southern coast of England. A new north-west force would extend from the Mersey to the Pennines, covering Greater Manchester, Merseyside and Lancashire, as well as swallowing up smaller forces such as Cheshire and Cumbria.
One chief constable told the Guardian: “Everyone knows 43 forces have to go. But the return on investment could take five or six years.”
Another chief constable said: “If I was the chief constable of the super force, it would be such a huge area, I wouldn’t know anybody. I worry about it being too big.”
Matthew Scott, the Conservative police and crime commissioner for Kent, said: “They will spend a great deal of time tearing up the fabric of policing for a suboptimal outcome.” The government plans to abolish PCCs as part of its changes.
Another police leader asked: “Where is the evidence bigger forces are better?” They cited the fact that in recent years the largest – such as the Met, Greater Manchester and West Midlands – had failed so badly they had been put into special measures and their chief constables or commissioners had been ousted.
Scotland and Northern Ireland are each already covered by a single force.

title: Cristiano Ronaldo announces retirement from international football
content_c:
Cristiano Ronaldo retires from international football
November 5, 2026
Cristiano Ronaldo took to social media on Thursday to announce that he had played his last game for Portugal.
"To the Portuguese people, the day has come for me to hand back the No. 7 shirt of our national team," the 41-year-old Ronaldo said in a video on his Instagram account.
"I never felt it belonged to me alone, but for 23 years I had the privilege and the responsibility of wearing it, defending it and carrying it with me into stadiums all around the world," Ronaldo said.
The former Manchester United, Real Madrid and Juventus forward represented his country 234 times, scoring 146 goals — making him the men's record-holder for international appearances and for international goals.
Decision made with 'head and heart'
He captained Portugal to their first major trophy at Euro 2016 and led them to the 2019 and 2025 Nations League titles.
"It was not an easy decision, there are decisions that are not only with the head. They are also made with the heart," Ronaldo continued in the Instagram post.
"If I ever made you happy, if one of my goals ever made you hug someone, forget a worry or feel proud of our country, then it was all worth it."
He also thanked his family, the Portuguese people and the teammates, coaches and staff he worked with over his national team career.
'The greatest of all time'
The Portuguese Football Association (FPF) released a statement expressing its gratitude and respect for the player also known as "CR7."
"Cristiano Ronaldo has raised Portugal's profile and inspired generations of young people who dream of following in his footsteps; for many of us, he is the greatest player of all time!" it read.
The FPF intends to organize a tribute "in which the fans and the country can one more time applaud and celebrate a player who has given us so much."
Training camp walkout
While his long-rival Lionel Messi ended his Argentina career with a much anticipated farewell match last month, Ronaldo's final appearance may go down as Portugal's 1-0 win over Wales on September 24, depending on the nature of the tribute. Portugal coach Jorge Jesus left him on the bench for the following match and said he wouldn't start the next one.
Ronaldo responded by walking out of the Portugal training camp. He was subsequently suspended and fined by the FPF, but he had been expected to return to Portugal for the November international break.
Like Messi, Ronaldo intends to continue his club career with Al-Nassr in Saudi Arabia.
description: The announcement by the footballing legend comes just weeks after a public spat with Portugal coach Jorge Jesus over playing time.
